Arsenal's David Raya is second on the list with 80%, while Pickford lies sixth with a 73.7% save percentage, and the Everton man has also made fewer saves in total; 28 to Trafford's 37.

#1956. Ex-refs chief drops verdict on 'nailed-on' Vanja Dragojevic controversy away from Rangers

Rangers' Vanja Dragojevic was unfortunate to be sent off during Serbia's 3-1 defeat to Germany in the Nations League.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that a yellow card would have sufficed on Friday, 13 November.

The 20-year-old midfielder, much like his time at Ibrox so far, was forced to watch from the bench until being subbed on at the half-time break.

In the 74th minute, however, after a challenge on Joshua Kimmich and a VAR review, he was given his marching orders as Serbia fell to defeat.

Bayern Munich's star was left in a lot of pain following the collision, but upon review, it didn't look nearly as dangerous as it did initially.

Nonetheless, Serbia were forced to finish the game with nine men after another sending-off, but the Rangers man can feel hard done by.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett expected a simple caution to be enough, rather than sending Dragojevic off.

"Challenges where the landing foot lands on the Achilles of the opponent, that does endanger the safety of the opponent," he said.

"For me, there doesn't appear to be the excessive force to meet the criteria for serious foul play, and I think that's where the judgment of the referee has come in.

"I'd question that as a red card. I think it's a nailed-on, reckless card, for sure. I don't think I can fully criticise him for issuing a red card.

"But I think from an English point of view, we'd expect that to be yellow."

Dragojevic has made eight appearances for the Gers since signing from Partizan Beograd on a £4.6million deal.

Only three of them have been starts, but Football Insider understands that there are no current plans to send him out on loan in January.

However, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Keith Wyness believes that it is simply a matter of time before the player seeks an exit already.

Dragojevic would have wanted regular time when signing across the dotted line at Ibrox, but his spell has been anything but positive.

Manchester United are reportedly set to face competition from La Liga giants Barcelona for Manchester City left-back Rayan Ait-Nouri.

The Algerian is on the fringes of Maresca's first-team plans, and an exit in January is highly on the cards.

Alejandro Balde, who was linked with a move to Man Utd in the summer, remains another option at left-back, but he could be on the move in a few months time due to lack of game time.

Barcelona are looking at a profile like Ait-Nouri, who is an attacking left-back with loads of experience under his belt, and could make a move for him in January.

#1952. Official: RedBird launch ‘Milan Sports & Entertainment’ company – the initial focuses

Today, RedBird Capital Partners have announced the creation of a new company that will focus specifically on AC Milan.

This season, Gerry Cardinale’s commitments to Milan have been seen much more. The American has been at every game in Serie A, proving his desire to be closer to the team and it feels like his relationship with the club (and fans) is growing deeper.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He’s still got room to learn, but it’s a substantial improvement from recent years and now, he’s taken a new step forward.

As MilanNews relays, RedBird Capital Partners have now launched a new holding company for anything and everything related to the Rossoneri, calling ‘Milan Sports & Entertainment’, MSE for short.

This company will ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’ and organise individual assets into a ‘multi-sport platform’.

The report continues, stating that MSE will help to further transform Milano into one of the ‘most influential sports and entertainment markets in the world’ by combining its importance in fashion, design, culture, sports and entertainment.

Above all, though, it’s another representation of RedBird’s long-term investment and commitment to the club (and the city).

San Donato is also referenced, with MSE making a commitment to the area, and there are plans to create a stadium and arena management business, which could eventually culminate in the Rossoneri’s NBA team.

Finally, RedBird have formed a new leadership team for the group, with Brett Yormark appointed the CEO of the company. He will report directly to Cardinale and will lead the ‘development and implementation of MSE’s strategy, overseeing current portfolio businesses and evaluating future investment opportunities.’

#1950. Liverpool backed to finalise Virgil van Dijk deal after confession - Transfer expert

Virgil van Dijk has been backed to sign a new contract at Liverpool after he confessed he would be happy to extend his stay.

The 35-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season, and it has been suggested that Liverpool could be prepared to let him move on, but his latest comments have changed things.

While he explained that no agreement is close, and they are in no rush to force things through, there is also no panic or concern about his contract situation at Anfield.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Van Dijk's words will have eased pressure on Liverpool, who plan to offer him a new deal in due course.

The Netherlands international remains a crucial part of Andoni Iraola's ambitious plans for success, both on the pitch and behinid the scenes, and his exit would come as a blow.

Van Dijk's reveal that he is happy to stay and extend his contract at Liverpool will now calm a lot of nerves, with all parties now able to look towards the future.

Football Insider revealed last month that Liverpool will be prepared to offer Van Dijk a new contract if he can continue to prove himself to Iraola this season.

The legendary defender has little to prove with regard to his influence, but given his age, concerns have crept in about how much longer he can play at the top level.

But having impressed so far this season, he remains part of the manager's long-term plans, and there is a growing possibility that Van Dijk will be offered a new contract.

"It seems like Van Dijk wants to stay at Liverpool, and that's got to come as a boost," Brown told Football Insider.

"He's still a top-class defender, he's part of the team and playing every week, and he's showing he still has plenty to contribute in the Premier League.

"Obviously there are a few concerns about his age, he's 35 now so it might not be long before he starts to drop off, but he's just as big of an influence behind the scenes.

"When you have somebody like Van Dijk on the books, you want to keep him around for as long as possible, because he offers so much both on and off the pitch.

"After he's come out and said he would be willing to stick around, it's a no-brainer really for Liverpool to offer him a new contract."

Despite the news that Van Dijk is willing to sign a new contract at Liverpool, work has also been ongoing behind the scenes to identify a long-term replacement at the back.

Regardless of his importance to the side, the Netherlands international is now 35 years old, and plans are being made for the future in case his form faces a drop off.

Football Insider revealed on 14 November that Liverpool are keeping a close eye on the progress of Ismaelo Ganiou, who has impressed in Ligue 1 with Lens in recent months.

The 21-year-old is viewed as one of the best young defensive talents in Europe, and despite having only recently signed a new contract, could be available for the right price.

Jeremy Jacquet arrived from France in the summer and has been incredibly impressive, and Liverpool could now follow that blueprint and up their interest in landing Ganiou.

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 14 Nov 2026 21:52, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 11:43

Namibia will be looking to revive their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations when they host Cameroon in Gaborone on Monday afternoon, four days after losing the first leg of their Group G double-header.

The Indomitable Lions claimed a 2-0 victory when the sides met on Thursday, leaving them three points clear at the top of the section, and another win would secure their place at the finals.

Cameroon are now one win away from reaching the AFCON finals for the 23rd time and a seventh consecutive tournament, with their resilient form playing a key role in their qualification campaign.

After recording a victory in the second match of March's biennial FIFA Series, the Indomitable Lions have collected seven points from their opening three qualifying games, including a first-round win over Comoros and a draw with Congo.

Thursday's first-leg triumph over Namibia came courtesy of first-half strikes from Saidou Alioum and Bil Nsongo, meaning David Pagou's side have scored at least twice in three of their last five outings.

Cameroon have also kept clean sheets in three matches during that period, including a 1-0 friendly victory over Ivory Coast on October 3, 2026, and the West-Central African nation, currently 42nd in the FIFA World Rankings, will look to maintain that form on Monday.

The Indomitable Lions have also been solid on the road, losing just one of their last eight matches outside their own country while winning five, and they have avoided defeat in each of their most recent three outings in that run.

Namibia, meanwhile, have seen their bid to reach the AFCON finals for only the fifth time and a second in the last three editions become more difficult, with Thursday's defeat leaving the Brave Warriors one point behind second place after Comoros drew with Congo.

The result also means Collin Benjamin's side have now lost each of their last three outings across all competitions, failing to score in any of them since their 1-0 victory over Congo in the opening round of the qualifiers.

The Brave Warriors have also been shaky defensively during that period, conceding nine goals across those three matches, including six in a friendly defeat to Russia after losing 1-0 to Comoros.

There is, however, some encouragement in the fact that Namibia have lost just one of their last five competitive matches as the designated hosts, winning the most recent two such outings.

Namibia have struggled in this fixture, though, losing four of their previous seven meetings (W1, D2) across all competitions, although their most recent home encounter with the Indomitable Lions ended in a goalless draw.

Cameroon Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Experienced figures Deon Hotto, Riaan Hanamub and Peter Shalulile are expected to feature again as Benjamin looks for a response from his side.

Cameroon remain without Carlos Baleba and Christian Kofane, who both withdrew before the first leg due to injuries sustained at their respective clubs.

Meanwhile, Mahamadou Nagida is available again after serving his suspension in the first leg, while Bryan Mbeumo could retain his place on the left side of attack after providing an assist last time out.

#1941. Somalia vs Ghana - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 14 Nov 2026 22:11

After claiming their first victory of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign in the opening leg at Essipong Sports Stadium, Ghana will be the nominal visitors when they face Somalia at the same venue in Monday afternoon's return fixture of their Group C double-header.

The Black Stars secured a 2-0 win when the sides met on Thursday, leaving them third in the section, six points behind leaders Ivory Coast, three adrift of second-placed Gambia and three ahead of Monday's designated hosts, who remain bottom without a point.

Ghana will be looking to record back-to-back victories for the first time in their qualifying campaign after a difficult start saw them lose to Ivory Coast and Gambia in September.

The Black Stars suffered a 2-0 defeat in Abidjan before surrendering a two-goal lead in a 4-2 home loss to Gambia, results that contributed to Carlos Queiroz's departure and left interim coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren with plenty of work to do.

Thursday's victory over Somalia offered some encouragement, with Jonas Adjetey opening the scoring shortly before halftime after Jordan Ayew had missed a penalty, before Felix Afena-Gyan added a second after the break.

The result also marked Bjorkegren's first competitive win in charge and Ghana's first AFCON qualifying victory in about three years, having missed out on the previous continental finals after a disappointing campaign.

Having also ended a five-match winless run last time out, the Black Stars will now be looking to secure consecutive victories for the first time since September and October 2025, with their only other win in their last 13 outings across all competitions coming against Panama in the World Cup group stage.

Somalia, meanwhile, have managed just one goal across their last six outings in all competitions, while losing each of their AFCON qualifying matches since progressing beyond the preliminary round with a penalty shootout victory over Mauritius.

Yusuf Ali Nur's team have conceded exactly twice in each of those qualifiers, losing 2-1 to Gambia in the opening round and 2-0 to Ivory Coast on matchday two before Thursday's defeat to Ghana.

Another loss on Monday would leave the Ocean Stars' hopes of reaching the continental finals for the first time hanging by a thread, with the side currently ranked a lowly 200th in the FIFA World Rankings facing a daunting task against opponents sitting 130 places higher.

There is little encouragement to draw from previous meetings, as Somalia have lost all three of their encounters with Ghana, conceding multiple goals each time while failing to find the net.

Ghana will be without Antoine Semenyo and Jan Gyamerah, who are both unavailable through injury, while no suspensions have been confirmed.

Thomas Partey, Mohammed Kudus, Mohammed Salisu and captain Jordan Ayew all returned to the squad for the double-header, with the latter three expected to feature again after Thursday's victory.

#1939. Cardinale discusses MSE creation and evolution within Milan: “Helping write a new chapter”

With the news of the new company leading AC Milan, Gerry Cardinale has offered a few words about what it means for the project.

In recent minutes, RedBird have announced a new parent company for Milan, aptly named ‘Milan Sports & Entertainment’. It’s a project that aims to put all of the club’s investments under one umbrella, whilst also allowing further investment into the city.

The new stadium is believed to have played a big part in this decision, and the Rossoneri will hopefully benefit significantly from this move.

As MilanNews relays, Cardinale offered some words in the announcement about the creation of the company, what it means to the city and for Rossoneri fans, what it means for the club.

“Over the past 25 years, we have worked alongside rights holders in the sports and media sectors to create innovative businesses that have transformed their respective industries.

“This evolution is based on a deep respect for the intellectual property assets that underpin these businesses, a long-term partnership with rights holders, and the ambition to fully unlock the potential of these teams and leagues, both on and off the pitch.

“Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the culmination of this journey and the work we have carried out since we first invested in AC Milan four years ago. Becoming a club owner has given us an even deeper understanding of what creates long-term value: winning, serving fans, and investing in the communities that give these institutions meaning.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

Considering how much attention Cardinale has paid to the future of the Diavolo, and taking them back to the top level, it’s nice to hear it referenced once again in his latest statement. Hopefully this move is another step towards that.

#1937. Bognor Regis Town take derby honours as Littlehampton Town are edged out

It was a first win in five for Danny Hollands’ team and left them third in the table and just a point behind leaders Jersey Bulls, who they visit at the end of the month.

A lively start saw Golds player-joint manager George Gaskin closed down at one end – then Luke Roberts set Ben Sheaf away on the left but his cross was wayward.

On seven minutes Sheaf put the ball inside to Henry McDonald and he hit a shot on the turn and low. Billy Collings did well though to divert it wide.

Ethan Robb latched on to a ball in midfield and picked out Roberts on the left but after speeding down the wing his cross flew over the bar. In 17 minutes Cal Laycock found Roberts and he sped on before shooting wide from the edge of the box.

Golds’ Harry Heath was a nuisance and forced a save from Tommy Scott at his near post. Then Matthew Storm lost possession to Laycock who ran through into the box but his strike was easily saved on 27 minutes.

Benny Read – a new Rocks signing from Gosport – made a mistake as Dion Jarvis stole the ball before picking out Gaskin but with only Scott to beat, he hit it straight at the keeper.

Jarvis and Robb were booked after a tackle by Bognor's defensive midfielder. Heath also went into the book and Sheaf had to come off with what looked like a hamstring injury. Harvey Whyte replaced him on 37 minutes.

Bognor went close in the second minute of first half stoppage time. Henry Nevill worked himself the box but his shot crashed off the post.

It didn't take long for Bognor to take the lead in the second half. Read put a pass inside to Laycock and he had beaten the offside trap and turned and coolly slotted the ball into the bottom corner on 47 minutes.

Scott Faber lashed out with a challenge on Robb and went into the book on 57 minutes.

Bognor extended their lead in the 59th minute as Josh Batt lashed a loose ball into the net on the half-volley after a long free-kick by Kaya Tshaka.

On 64 minutes Bognor made a double change as Laycock and McDonald made way for Oliver Lovell and Charlie Gunson.

The Golds got a goal back directly from a corner as Gaskin headed in from a 69th minute delivery. Then Gaskin put in a dangerous ball across from the left but Lewis Olajide flashed it wide.

Jarvis blasted over as Littlehampton swung the momentum to their advantage.

Ben Anderson and Louie Williams replaced Robb and Read for Bognor in the 76th minute.

Tshaka was battling in midfeld and was unlucky to lose possession. A long ball saw Heath run powerfully into the area but Scott was quick out of his goal to bravely stop him.

Williams was booked for simulation on 87 minutes as he seemed to lost his footing in the box.

It was a real battle in the closing moments as Williams was holding up the ball for Bognor where he could. But Littlehampton posed a threat with some quick play and long throws from the dangerous Heath.

Five minutes were added but Bognor held on to move third in the division.

#1933. Lithuania vs Liechtenstein - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 14 Nov 2026 22:55

Lithuania welcome Liechtenstein to the Darius and Girenas Stadium on Monday evening for the final round of League D fixtures in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Trispalves fell to a narrow 1-0 defeat against Azerbaijan, while Blau-Rot lost to Milli Komanda by the same scoreline on Friday evening.

After suffering relegation from League C in their 2024-25 Nations League endeavours, finishing bottom of Group 2 having failed to pick up a single point from their six matches, Lithuania will be fairly content with how they have performed in the competition over the previous few months.

Trispalves positively kick-started their campaign by beating Monday’s opposition away from home in their opening encounter before drawing with Azerbaijan, but after falling to a 1-0 defeat against the latter in their most recent outing, they are sat four points behind Odlar Yurdu, who have guaranteed top spot.

Alongside this, Lithuania also endured heartbreak in their latest pursuit of the Baltic Cup, as following a penalty shootout victory over Latvia in the semifinals, Trispalves conceded late on to fall short against Estonia in the final and as a result failed to end their 16-year wait for a competition title.

While every League D nation is guaranteed promotion at the end of play on Monday, with the division being completely abolished ahead of the 2028-29 campaign, Mindaugas Cepas’s men will certainly want to avoid finishing at the foot of the standings after facing Liechtenstein, who they have bizarrely beaten 2-0 in each of the previous three meetings between the sides.

Following a damning World Cup qualification campaign in which they lost all of their eight Group J games and failed to score a single goal, conceding a huge 31 in the process, Liechtenstein have also weathered a deflating set of Nations League fixtures.

Having been beaten 2-0 by Lithuania in their first match, Konrad Funfstuck’s men did well to steady the ship and play out a score draw with table-toppers Azerbaijan, but after falling to a slim defeat against Odlar Yurdu on Friday evening, the visitors head into Monday’s clash requiring victory by three goals in order to climb off the foot of the standings.

To do so, Blau-Rot will certainly have to discover some attacking threat though, having not won by more than a two-goal margin since October 2007 and currently in an extremely rough patch of form, losing 19 of their latest 21 outings in all competitions.

Although they do not boast the best record against Lithuania, losing six of their prior eight meetings with Trispalves, Liechtenstein do have experience of overcoming Monday’s hosts, beating them 2-0 at Rheinpark Stadion in June 2011.

Having been shown a straight red card against Azerbaijan last month, 23-year-old forward Armandas Kucys will miss this week’s match for Lithuania and could be replaced by either Ignas Venckus or Edgaras Dubickas in attack.

After their victory against Blau-Rot last time out, it would be no surprise to see the hosts revert back to having three in midfield, with Lukas Michelbrink and Torino’s Gvidas Gineitis both likely to feature.

Although they kept a clean sheet with five in defence against Suriname on Thursday evening, it is likely that Trispalves deploy a back four this time out, with Justas Lasickas captaining the side from left-back.

Liechtenstein have a fully fit squad to choose from on Monday night as goalkeeper Tim-Tiado Oehri returns from a lengthy ACL injury and 19-year-old defender Yonas Abido receives his first call-up to the national side.

Hoping to net their first goal of the campaign in the final fixture, the only nation alongside Georgia still yet to have scored with one match remaining, Blau-Rot’s chances of ending their rut could well be down to Fabio Luque-Notaro and Alessandro Lo Russo, who are likely to form the visitors’ strike partnership this week.

Bartkus; Sirvys, Kazukolovas, Utkus, Lasickas; Gineitis, Vorobjovas, Michelbrink; Jankauskas, Dubickas, Venckus

With nothing to lose, Liechtenstein will be gunning to end their Nations League campaign on a high and claim their first victory over Lithuania in 15 years.

However, facing a Trispalves side who have lost just one of their previous five matches and took all three points when the nations met in September, it is difficult to see that happening and we predict the hosts to confirm a second-placed finish by winning on Monday evening.

Jordan Young gave the away side a half-time advantage with a well-taken effort on 17 minutes, but the Rebels backline could not quitewithstand the Iron’s second half resurgence and Eastbourne-raised Norwood came up with the late leveller for new boss Andy Preece.

Returning after an 11-day break from action, the side featured two changes to the eleven that began the 3-0 defeat by Sutton United in their last league outing.

Harrison Foulkes regained his place in goal while Charlie Waller returned to the defensive unit. New signing Sam Clucas featured on the bench, with Daniel Isichei also named amongst the substitutes.

A sense of optimism among the home faithful in Preece’s first game at the helm was combatted by a strong start from the away side, spearheaded by the dynamic movement of Young to initiate some promising moves early on.

Having asserted themselves on the ball through the opening quarter of an hour, the Rebels found the breakthrough in the 17th minute. Brilliant link-up between Kendall and Young saw the latter pick up the ball in a central position just outside the box. The former Torquay United man let off a fierce low effort on his left side which clipped off the foot of Maison Campbell’s left post before nestling inside the opposite upright.

The movement of Razzaq Coleman De-Graft and Young to pick up space behind the Iron midfield gave the away side a constant outlet on the break, from which they were able to fashion several dangerous breakaways.

The Rebels’ counter-attacking prowess remained their best route towards goal heading into the break, with Kendall having a good chance to double the visitors’ lead 90 seconds before the interval.

After jinking away from one challenge at the edge of the box, the forward drilled a low effort narrowly wide of the mark down to Campbell’s left-hand side.

Having grown into the game towards the end of the first 45 minutes, Preece’s hosts started the second half with renewed intensity, keeping play largely in the Worthing half as Adam Hinshelwood’s side were forced to defend their box.

Alfie Beestin had two attempts on goal, first being denied by Foulkes from a long throw before having a strike blocked from around 20 yards.

The attacking movement and nuisance of Norwood lent itself to Scunthorpe’s direct approach to getting back level, with the former Oldham striker constantly winning first balls.

Just after the hour mark, Pat Jones’ delivery from the right flank was stabbed over the bar by Norwood at the edge of the six-yard box, as tight defending from Joe Cook and Jayden Moore prevented the veteran from getting a more telling touch.

Pressure continued to mount on Worthing with minutes ticking away. With two minutes of the 90 to play, the Attis Arena was plunged into momentary silence as substitute Declan Howe’s header deflected agonisingly wide.

With 30 seconds remaining of three additional minutes, all the resolute defending from the visitors came undone as Scunthorpe found a leveller. After the away side surrendered possession inside their own half, Howe’s clipped ball towards the back post was headed back across goal and eventually poked home by Norwood.

It was a gutting conclusion from a Rebels perspective, especially for Foulkes, who commanded his box astutely through numerous waves of lofted deliveries into the area.

By Lewis Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 23:27

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai has confirmed that he was close to suffering an injury while playing for Hungary.

The Reds star was part of the Hungarian XI that beat Georgia 2-0 in the Nations League on Saturday, registering an assist.

Many Reds fans were worried about the 26-year-old's fitness given Andoni Iraola had expressed concern about a potential injury heading into the international break.

Szoboszlai fuelled those fears after admitting he was close to pulling out of Saturday's match, telling reporters: "During the warm-up I was close to saying that I wouldn't be able to play after all. I felt the injury during one of my shots, but I thought to myself that, having come this far, I wasn't going to let the team down.

"So I tried to give everything I had, as best as I could. My leg felt good, but now the treatment process starts all over again, and I need to be ready for Tuesday."

Szoboszlai has struggled hamstring and knee issues this season, and Liverpool will want him to sit out of his nation's clash with Northern Ireland on Tuesday given the Reds will face Manchester United in the Premier League on November 22.

While Szoboszlai has not played particularly well this season for the Reds, he is one of just three senior options for midfield.

Losing him for an extended period of time would leave Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch as the only experienced stars for Iraola to choose from, but the latter has not been trusted by the head coach in 2026-27.

Though youngster Trey Nyoni should arguably be in the Reds' starting XI irrespective of injury concerns, the 19-year-old cannot be expected to start on a consistent basis.

Given Szoboszlai has already suffered two injuries this campaign, further minutes this international break would be a major concern ahead of the busy winter period.

With depth a serious issue for Iraola, it should come as no surprise to see the club linked to midfielders ahead of the January transfer window.

Lamine Camara has often been touted as a target for the Merseysiders, and his abilities with and without the ball would make him a strong addition.

The 22-year-old would ensure that Nyoni is not overplayed, while also allowing Szoboszlai to avoid being forced into the XI should his injury issues persist.

Whether Liverpool act on any interest in January remains to be seen, but it would be risky to head into the rest of the campaign with the same options in midfield.

#1925. 'No point' - Former QPR and Charlton striker has say on Crawley Town strategy for next manager

That’s the view of former QPR and Charlton striker Conor Washington as he has his say on Crawley Town’s next managerial appointment.

Reds owners have yet to name a permanent successor for Colin Kazim-Richards, who was sacked on October 21 following a poor start to the season which has sees them rock bottom of League Two.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Kevin Blackwell has been in charge on an interim basis but Reds fans are eagerly anticipating who will be the next permanent boss as they look to climb the table.

But Washington, in his latest exclusive EFL column for BestBettingBonuses.co.uk, says there is a bigger picture at play.

“I think the bigger question for me is around the overall football strategy at the club,” he said. “With the structure they've got, they either need to decide on a clear way they want the club to play, recruit players who fit that and then appoint managers who can implement it, or they need to appoint a manager with a really clear playing style and back him with recruitment that suits what he's trying to do. Both approaches can work, but you can't really keep moving between the two.

"Otherwise you end up with players recruited for one manager being asked to play a completely different way under the next one.

“From what Colin Kazim-Richards said in the summer, there was clearly an attempt to recruit players specifically for his ideas, but now they're potentially looking for another manager just a few months later. That's where the problems can start.”

And he added that it’s a big job for whoever comes in. He said: “I think whoever comes in needs to be really clear about what they've inherited, what the players are actually capable of and how they can get the best out of them.

"There's no point appointing someone because you like their philosophy if the squad isn't equipped to carry it out, particularly when you're fighting to stay in the league.”

#1924. There's still a place in the modern game for managers like Kevin Blackwell, says former Hearts and Rotherham United striker

Kevin Blackwell has been in charge of Crawley Town on an interim basis since the end of October following the sacking on Colin Kazim-Richards after a terrible start to the season for the Reds.

The 67-year-old has a vast amount of managerial experience including jobs at Leeds United and Sheffield United and, despite an embarrassing exit in the FA Cup to seventh tier Wimborne Town, has had a good start to his Reds stint with four points in two league games.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

And Washington, in his latest exclusive EFL column for BestBettingBonuses.co.uk, is happy to see Blackwell involved.

“I think it's great to see genuine football people like Kevin still involved in the game,” he said. “Football feels very modern and young at the minute, and sometimes it seems like coaches are inventing new vocabulary every other week to describe things we've been doing for decades!

“The reality is that so much of what we're seeing tactically has been done before in some way, shape or form. Of course the game evolves and you have to adapt with it, but the fundamental aim of football hasn't changed.”

And he added that experience can be seen as detrimental sometimes when it comes to older managers. He said: “So much of management is still about understanding people, building relationships and helping players through difficult situations. I think we're sometimes too quick to dismiss experienced managers or label them as dinosaurs because they might talk about defending deep rather than playing in a low block.

" Ultimately, they're describing the same thing, and just because someone doesn't use the latest terminology doesn't mean they don't understand the game.”

But Washington said experience is what Reds need right now. “In Crawley's situation, I think having someone who's experienced difficult periods before and isn't afraid to be demanding could be exactly what the players need,” he said.

"That doesn't necessarily mean being abrasive for the sake of it, but sometimes players need clarity, honesty and someone who's prepared to make difficult decisions.”

But should Blackwell be considered for the job permanently? Washington said: “I think that should come down to the impact he has on the players and the results he gets, rather than any preconceived ideas about his style or personality.

"There's absolutely still a place in the modern game for managers like Kevin, and I think it would be a shame if we lost sight of that.”

#1923. Estonia vs Bulgaria - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 14 Nov 2026 23:32, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 02:37

Estonia will welcome Bulgaria to the Lillekula Stadium in Tallinn for Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The hosts, who have secured a top-two finish, could still achieve automatic promotion, while the visitors only have pride to play for on the final matchday of the league phase.

Having been in the bottom two tiers for all five editions of the Nations League, Estonia have put themselves in a position to win promotion to League B for the very first time.

Jurgen Henn's side are guaranteed at least a promotion playoff spot after winning the draw and drawing three of their five matches in Group 4C.

In fact, they have recorded four consecutive shutouts since playing out a 1-1 draw with Iceland on the first matchday.

Their latest clean sheet enabled them to pick up a 1-0 victory in Saturday's away clash against Luxembourg, which came courtesy of Maksim Paskotsi's second goal of the 2026-27 Nations League campaign.

Sitting in second spot and two points adrift of Iceland, Estonia know they need a win and Luxembourg to claim three points in Reykjavik if they are to snatch automatic promotion on the final matchday.

That would require Estonia to pick up their first-ever win against Bulgaria, having drawn two and lost one of their previous three meetings.

Bulgaria already know they will be competing in League C next time around after falling hopelessly short in their promotion bid, mustering just four points from their five matches in Group C4.

After taking just a point from their first three games, Bulgaria finally ended their five-game winless run in all internationals with a 2-0 away victory over Luxembourg in their final outing of the September/October international break.

However, they failed to build upon that result in their most recent outing against Iceland, as they slumped to a demoralising 5-0 defeat in Plovdiv, ensuring they will end the league phase without a home win to their name.

While they cannot finish any higher than third, the Lions are still at risk of dropping to the bottom of the group, with just a point separating them from Luxembourg in fourth position.

Bulgaria may be unbeaten in three meetings against Estonia, but they had to settle for a goalless draw in their only previous away encounter in European Championship qualifying in April 2003.

Their hopes of troubling the scorers on this occasion may be tempered by the fact they have failed to score in three of their last four outings, including a stalemate in September's reverse fixture between these two nations.

Henn could opt for consistency by naming the same lineup that started Friday's narrow win over Luxembourg.

Friday's match-winner Paskotsi will feature alongside Erko Tougjas and Karol Mets in central defence, while Rasmus Peetson and Michael Schjonning-Larsen are set to operate as the two wing-backs.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Patrik Kristal will lead the line with Mattias Mannilaan, who is aiming to bring his club form to the international stage after netting five goals in his last four games for Kalju.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Martin Minchev, who withdrew from the squad last week due to injury.

With Ribarski likely to make alterations, Ivan Turitsov and Dimitar Velkovski are in contention to feature in the backline on Monday.

Martin Petkov, Ivaylo Chochev and Georgi Lazarov are also among those who could come into Ribarski's thinking.

"It’s important we don’t dwell on the what ifs dust ourselves off and go again. Its points dropped, another defeat on the road and we can’t hide from the fact that ultimately our away form is not good enough and is something we must look to rectify quickly.”

Spirited Yapton were generally second-best, but had their moments, especially in the first half.

They trailed in the third minute when a Bosham corner to the far post was neatly headed home. Then Yapton's best efforts were shots from Aaron Tague and Josh Dean that were respectively well saved and scrambled off the line.

Early in the second period Brandon Terry equalised with a superb cross-shot but from that point Bosham took over with some impressive approach work and wrapped it up with goals in the 70th and 85th minutes.

#1921. Thoughts of a lifelong fan: Fingers-crossed for a first home win and a night off for Kabby

I am just about getting over our exit from the FA Cup and the Jersey Mike’s Trophy, watching Exeter City go one up against CTFC (the other one), and in visiting OUR club’s website I was shocked to see we only have just over an hour to go before we play Rotherham away.

We don’t of course, because of international call ups for both sides. The three for Crawley being Dion Pereira, Stephen Duke-McKenna and Nick Michalski. Dion played for 60 minutes for Antigua and Barbuda in a 3-2 home defeat, whilst Nick was in goal for the England U20 side in  a 6-1 win against Czechia and Stephen was scoring a brace for Guyana in a six nil away victory over the Cayman Islands. I hope it’s not too long before he is scoring again for Crawley.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Going back to "us” playing at Rotherham, and with just 40 minutes to kick off, “I follow” will sell you an audio pass to the game if you want to listen, surely this rivals the notice board outside the Broadfield stadium in not showing the club in the best light. In the old days, and I know this makes me sound like everyone’s dad or Uncle Albert, Stan Markham would have the next match on the board at half time while people were still watching the game and we didn't have the internet, but I'm sure we wouldn’t have been advertising something that wasn’t going to take place.

Of course, you can hope for things as much as you want, doesn’t mean that it will happen though, but out of the nine top half v bottom half matches taking place only Colchester United, Port Vale and Fleetwood of the bottom half teams achieved victories. Roch In the weekends League 2 games, which were all on the tele because of the international window, Exeter hung on to beat Cheltenham by one goal to nil in the early game and then, because Joe Comper works for Gillingham and Jay Williams plays for Colchester, I decided to watch that one and of course, was cheering on the Kent side. In all the matches taking place there appears to be an almost top half versus bottom half feel to the fixtures and, because of the predicament we are currently in.

I have to say it would have been really good if the results had gone to form. Jay missed a sitter for the team from Essex in the first half, then got booked for a very robust tackle, which, if it had been committed in a red shirt would probably have got him sent off. Two goals in the second half saw the team I wanted to lose, win their first game in ten so now it was down to the others to perform to my script. Rochdale, Swindon, Bristol Rovers and Oldham all lost, and the Cobblers drew at Salford and Newport drew at Crewe after leading by two goals to nil.

For those of us with short memories, who can’t remember a season where we have started so badly, we need only go back to last year when we sat on exactly the same number of points after the first 12 league games played. We have scored more this season, by three goals, but unfortunately have conceded more as well. In order to ensure we stay in the football league for next season everyone knows we need to start winning games and that is why, as supporters we need to do what it says on the tin and support the lads wearing our colours through all the games left this season. Last year in the next 14 games we won just 10 more points and in the whole season we won just eight games and still managed to survive on the last day of the season.

Hopefully, although Priestley Farquharson appears to be out of contention for a while because of the injury sustained in the defeat at Wimborne, the return of Josh Flint and the arrival of Ben Heneghan will strengthen our defence and Duke-McKenna will add some Guianan magic and start scoring goals for the Red Devils again like he did against Bromley back at the beginning of October and before you know it we’ll be climbing the league ladder to safety.

Can we do it?  Yes, we can, but it must start with us making sure we beat the teams around us rather than those destined at least for the play offs. Don’t get me wrong, I would gladly take three points off the likes of Barnet next Tuesday but the minimum we should expect is for a concerted effort from all those who play for or support this club of ours. Hopefully we will achieve our first home league win here on Saturday against Fleetwood and Kabby Tshimanga will have an off night next week and live up to my friend's opinion that he really isn’t that good.  I wouldn’t bank on that though as back in the day he also said something along the lines of “Paul Fishenden, he’ll never make a centre forward".

I’m going to sign off now, before the men in the white coats arrive, but before I do go for a well-earned Sunday dinner, I would like to say that I am giving up being an optimist for being hopeful. Have a read of the definitions below and see if you should become hopeful too.

Optimism is a generalized, passive expectation or belief that things will turn out well and that positive future outcomes are more likely than negative ones. It looks at the big picture and assumes the future will improve largely on its own, through luck, external circumstances, or the natural order of things.

Hope is an active, goal-directed motivational state. It requires acknowledging current difficulties, pain, or poor odds rather than ignoring them. Hope involves building concrete plans and agency (the personal energy and determination) to act and shape a better outcome, even when the odds are stacked against you. for

Thank you, Christina Cipriani, (Crawley URC) for showing me the light

Here endeth the sermon for this week. Noli Cedere, Never Give Up.

Scotland Under-21s rounded off their Spanish training camp with a 1-1 friendly draw against the United States Under-23 side at Pinatar Arena, as preparations for the upcoming European Championship qualifiers continued.

The Young Scots faced a stern test against an American outfit featuring six players with senior international experience and led by 87-cap former international Steven Cherundolo. The USA were using the fixture as an important step in their preparations for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Tony Docherty's side went into the contest in confident mood following an impressive 4-0 victory over Ukraine earlier in the week, looking to carry that momentum into their final fixture of the year in Murcia.

Their opponents presented a different challenge, bringing greater physical presence and experience to the encounter. However, Scotland proved more than a match for the Stars and Stripes, with St Mirren's Eseosa Sule scoring an 85th-minute equaliser to secure a share of the spoils.

Hearts striker James Wilson, who bagged a double against Ukraine on Thursday, featured in the starting line-up once again, alongside captain Tyler Fletcher, midfielders Lennon Miller and Kyle Ure, Andrew Tod of Dunfermline and Aberdeen full-back Mitchel Frame.

The fixture provided Docherty with another valuable opportunity to assess his much-changed squad as he builds towards the start of next year's qualification campaign. Reflecting on the benefits of the training camp, Docherty said: “We were delighted with the performance and the result in the game against Ukraine on Thursday. It is a credit to the players that they have been able to take on board so much information in such a short period of time.

“The game against the USA was another step up in quality for the group. They were taking on a more experienced side, but we wanted to challenge the players, and we wanted to see what they can do on and off the ball in different situations.”

#1917. Liverpool transfer news: 'Significant' interest in £29m centre-back as Andoni Iraola ponders future without Virgil van Dijk

By Lewis Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 23:43, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 01:33

Liverpool are keen on Lens centre-back Pierre Ismaelo Ganiou despite interest from a number of other clubs, the latest report has claimed.

The Premier League is now on pause for the November international break, and that has given Reds supporters the chance to assess the squad.

Andoni Iraola has made a positive start to life at Anfield, with the team's defence having notably improved, led by the likes of Virgil van Dijk and Ronald Araujo.

However, Van Djik has entered the final year of his contract, while Araujo is only on loan from Barcelona and could return to the Spanish side at the end of the season.

Amid uncertainty regarding the future of their defence, Football Insider report that the Reds are one of several clubs keen on signing Lens defender Ganiou, who is valued by Transfermarkt at just over £25m.

Ganiou does not have an extensive history of top-flight football considering he has played just 28 games in Ligue 1 in his entire career, though he has been impressive for Lens.

In five league matches for the French side this season, the 21-year-old has won 69% of his duels, including 73% of his ground duels.

Liverpool have typically looked to sign aerially dominant defenders, so while the Frenchman boasts an impressive 64% duel success rate in the air, he only averages 1.8 aerial duels won per game.

Van Dijk has won an average of 3.8 duels in the air in the league so far, while Jeremy Jacquet has won 2.6 aerial duels in the Premier League, and the Reds would almost certainly aim to get Ganiou closer to those figures.

While Van Dijk is 35 and is into the final year of his contract, he has shown no signs of physical decline, and he has expressed a desire to remain at Anfield.

If he was to extend his stay on Merseyside, the Reds may not need to delve into the market for another centre-back.

Joe Gomez is expected to leave, and he could be replaced in the squad by Araujo, which would then leave the club in need of a right-back.

Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni will be part of the squad for the coming seasons, while many believe that Ifeanyi Ndukwe could play a role for the team once his loan at Levante ends.

#1916. Who is Mario Frick? The new manager at Aberdeen who scored at Hampden, lost to Hibs and develops players

Mario Frick says he will create an environment at Aberdeen “where his players can thrive” after being appointed the next manager of the Pittodrie outfit.

Former Luzern boss Frick takes over from Stephen Robinson, who was sacked on Monday by Aberdeen with the team languishing in 11th place in the Premiership. The length of his contract has not been disclosed.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dons hierarchy have moved quickly to land his successor and after a week of interviews have settled on former Liechtenstein striker Frick, 52, who has been out of work since the summer after end a five-year spell in Switzerland with Luzern.

Frick has also managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz in his homeland. He will be assisted by Roman Matter, a 44-year-old Swiss coach who was also at Luzern. The pair are due to arrive in Aberdeen imminently ahead of Saturday’s league match against bottom club Kilmarnock.

“I'm excited to be joining Aberdeen FC,” said Frick. “It's a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

“Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.”

Chief executive Adrian Bevington revealed Frick was the “unanimous” choice of the Aberdeen board after going through a robust process to identify him.

“We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club,” said Bevington. “This appointment follows a thorough and extensive recruitment process led by [sporting director] Lutz Pfannenstiel and myself on behalf of the board, during which we spoke to a number of highly qualified candidates.

“Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

“Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.

“He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the Board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen Football Club forward.

“I would like to thank the board, in particular Willie Garner, and colleagues across the club for their diligence and support throughout this process.”

Pfannenstiel tipped Frick to have a “real impact at Pittodrie” and said his character will be crucial as the Dons look to climb the league table.

“I’m really pleased that we have been able to bring Mario Frick to Aberdeen,” said Pfannenstiel. “I have enormous respect for his football knowledge, leadership qualities and passion for the game.

“Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

“We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact. I’m looking forward to working closely with him.”

Born in the Swiss town of Chur, Frick carved out a playing career as a physical striker and holds the record number of caps for Liechtenstein, scoring 16 goals in 125 appearances. One of those strikes came at Hampden in a 2-1 defeat by Scotland in 2010.

Also deployed as a centre-half, Frick played for clubs such as FC Basel, FC Zürich, St. Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana before hanging up his boots in 2016 and moving into coaching.

At Vaduz, he secured promotion to the Swiss Super League, which earned him a move to Luzern. He spent five years with them, landing a fourth-placed finish. He faced Hibs in the 2024 Conference League, losing 5-3 on aggregate.

Frick most used formation with Vaduz and Luzern was a 4-4-2 diamond and he has carved out a reputation as a head coach who has developed younger players, most notably AC Milan and Switzerland midfielder Ardon Jashari.

#1914. ‘With the times’ Scotland boss won me over with surprise call - here’s why he’s different to Steve Clarke

Scotland striker Che Adams admits he was instantly won over by head coach Sebastien Pocognoli after a surprise FaceTime call from the Belgian when he was out injured last month.

Adams, 30, was ruled out of Pocognoli’s inaugural camp in October after picking up a thigh injury with club side Torino, but was restored to the Scotland starting XI for their 2-1 win over North Macedonia on Friday night, and registered an assist for the first of John McGinn’s two goals.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After being regular for former manager Steve Clarke during his seven year reign, Adams admits Scotland’s early performances under their new 38-year-old manager have been patchy so far. Still ironing out the teething issues often faced by teams in transition, he concedes they are yet to click, but says the squad believe in Pocognoli and his new methods.

Get our daily football newsletter by clicking here.

“The camps haven’t changed much but the manager is definitely more intense,” said Adams. “I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad. This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.

“With Steve [Clarke] you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well, but he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail, off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do. In the last camp when I was out injured he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

“Coming off a transitional period like we have just now, it’s difficult to know where you are and what you want to do. But all the boys here want to play for our country and do Scotland proud. I had no doubts about it, it’s good to get away from Italy for a while, be around some good lads.”

Striking trio Kieron Bowie, Oli McBurnie and Robbie Ure were all called into the squad by Pocognoli for last month’s Nations League games against Slovenia, North Macedonia and Switzerland, with Adams injured and Lyndon Dykes and George Hirst both left out.

With enhanced competition for a starting spot, the Torino hitman said the Belgian ensured he kept in contact with him during his injury layoff, revealing the unique method Pocognoli implemented with the team since he was appointed manager in August.

“I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,” said Adams. “He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT [Kieran Tierney] was out for a walk when he phoned him. He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that, but it’s good.

“The manager is with the times, really, he’s brought in his new ideas. He’s a few years younger and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play. It just takes time to click but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants. We have been together for a number of years now so we know each other’s game. You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice, we won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

“For me, it’s a bit different to what I’m used to at club level because that’s a little bit more free. I can roam where I want in and around the back line for my club, but I am enjoying it. When you’re playing with boys like John McGinn and Scott McTominay who have the creativity, that eye for goal and pass forward that you don’t really get at club level it is good.

“The gaffer wanted me to run deep on Friday as well, so nothing changed there. As games go on, stretching the opposition helps John and Scott get on the ball where they can hurt teams with their creativity. You can definitely see things are coming together, you could see how we were building up and playing out. You have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.”

#1913. Bexhill United maintain play-off push by beating Seaford Town

With an international break hitting the top-tier domestic game - and on a stunning bright, but cold, late autumn day - the Pirates’ biggest crowd of the season, 226, gathered at the Polegrove to see if Jay Skinner-Swain’s men could kick on with their impressive league campaign to date.

Early signs were encouraging. Ash Latuske, wide on the right, was impressive from the off and on just three minutes he opened the scoring. Jack Shonk brought down a high ball and squared it to Latuske in space in the box and he grabbed the chance to knock it in.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Seaford Town have had a mixed few months of league action but have managed to chalk up some decent results and they now set about trying to claw their way back into the game after the early setback. They opened up a decent chance on 25 minutes but Finn Holter in the Bexhill goal reacted sharply to make a good save.

Minutes later Theo Coombs came close to doubling the Pirates lead, his shot heading wide of the post after he was well set up by Ryan Moir from out on the left.

As the play shifted quickly back down the other end, the pendulum swung again as a Charlie Playford challenge was adjudged by the ref to warrant a penalty. There were few complaints and the Seaford man crashed the ball home to level the score.

It was disappointing for Bexhill, but the team picked themselves up and got back at it straight from the restart. The run-up to half-time saw a period of sustained Pirates pressure.

On 40 minutes Luke Donaldson struck an absolute peach of a volley which Josh Mitchell-Lake in the Seaford goal managed to get just enough of a touch on to divert it over the bar.

That was followed shortly after by an acrobatic volley from defender Dale Penn which just cleared the bar with the Polegrove willing it in as Penn continues his search for that elusive goal.

One all at half-time meant that there was plenty to do.

Coombs has developed a knack in recent weeks of scoring quality goals at crucial moments. Saturday added another to that tally. On 65 minutes he picked up the ball outside the box, surged forwards and drove home a quality finish from distance.

But there was plenty of action and controversy left in this contest and half an hour into the half the ref handed Donaldson a straight red for a first offence that he viewed as dangerous.

Bexhill had played a large chunk of their away game at Seaford with ten men in August and it seemed to inspire them then. Now it had the same effect.

Suddenly Bexhill shirts were everywhere, winning the ball and setting up a wave of attacks. The Pirates made that pressure count with sheer persistence from Shonk creating a chance for himself that he squeezed home from a tight angle.

As Seaford tried to make some use of their one-man advantage they were leaving large gaps at the back for Bexhill to exploit with Moir in particular making hay.

Just after the 90 minutes were up he drove a shot towards goal and, with the keeper out of position, a defender threw himself across the line and handled to stop a certain goal. Off he went with a red card and Shonk blasted in the spot kick.

Deep into injury time Moir came close to nailing the goal he deserved. Breaking clear, shrugging off a challenge and just failed to beat the keeper.

This was a great result for Bexhill in front of a bumper crowd and they aim to keep the momentum going with another home league clash against Midhurst and Easebourne on Saturday.

#1912. Germany vs Netherlands - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 10:15

Fighting for a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Germany are set to host League A's Group A2 leaders, the Netherlands, at Olympiastadion Berlin on Monday.

Die Mannschaft know that they likely need to win to progress, while Oranje are through barring an unprecedented swing in goal-difference.

Jurgen Klopp's Germany are pushing to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals for just the second time, but they face a tough test to reach the last eight.

Die Mannschaft are currently third in Group A2, level on eight points with Greece and three behind the Netherlands, and their chance to go through leans on the fact UEFA prioritises head-to-head points between tied teams.

Klopp's side were beaten 1-0 by the Azure and White on September 27 before drawing 0-0 with them on matchday four.

However, Ivan Jovanovic's men were hammered 7-0 by the Dutch on Friday, meaning that a German victory over the Netherlands on Monday would see them progress ahead of Greece regardless of their result against Serbia.

Die Mannschaft were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Oranje on matchday one, with Cody Gakpo equalising in second-half stoppage time to deny his former Liverpool manager maximum points.

Klopp's team have remained undefeated in the group since their loss to Greece, most recently beating Serbia 3-1 on Friday, when they raced into a 2-0 lead within the first 14 minutes thanks to an own-goal from Srdjan Babic and a follow-up by Florian Wirtz.

Meanwhile, Xavi's Netherlands have yet to taste defeat in the Nations League this term, and are in a commanding position at the top of their group going into the final matchday.

Leading with 11 points, Oranje's 7-0 demolition of Greece last time out - following a 2-2 draw on October 1 - means the only possibility of them finishing below the top two is if there is a dramatic 14-goal swing in the Azure and White's favour.

Xavi is without talismanic centre-back Virgil van Dijk this month, but his team were still able to keep their first clean sheet in the competition on Friday, while Tijani Reijnders's first-half hat-trick set the tone at the opposite end of the pitch.

However, it remains to be seen whether the Netherlands can repeat that attacking showcase in Germany, considering that they have won just one of their last six away clashes against Die Mannschaft.

On the other hand, Oranje are unbeaten in their past seven matches on the road, and last suffered a travelling defeat in a penalty shootout against Spain during the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2025, following a 5-5 aggregate draw.

Germany have no new injury issues to contend with, though they are missing Bayern Munich stars Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry due to respective muscle problems.

In their absence, Klopp could continue with Brajan Gruda, Florian Wirtz and Derry Scherhant behind Arsenal man Kai Havertz up top.

As for the Netherlands, they were forced to take off Frenkie De Jong at half time against Greece after he suffered back pain, and he has now left the national squad to return to Barcelona.

Teun Koopmeiners looks set to step in and fill the gap alongside Joey Veerman at the base of Xavi's midfield, while Tijani Reijnders operates in the number 10 role.

Further forward, Donyell Malen has been a standout for Roma this season with 12 goals across all competitions, and he will be keen to add to his goal against Greece while Cody Gakpo and Crysencio Summerville provide width.

Captain Virgil van Dijk has sat out this international break with complaints of physical discomfort, so expect to see Tottenham Hotspur's Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke start at centre-back.

Ter Stegen; Treu, Thiaw, Tah, Mittelstadt; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Gruda, Wirtz, Scherhant; Havertz

The maths of the table may be complex, but Germany know that a simple victory will see them through to the quarter-finals.

Oranje have yet to lose in the Nations League this season, though with the stakes lowered, they could be caught off guard.

#1911. Scotland face a mountainous task - but rewards are worth the climb

To emphasis the scale of what faces Scotland at the Sitterstadion in St Gallen on Monday night, the national team is looking to repeat a feat only carried out by Germany and Spain over the past two years.

Switzerland don’t lose often on home soil under Murat Yakin. The Germans and the world champions have prevailed in the Alps that period. In short, it takes a very good performance to leave with the full loot. And for Scotland to stand a chance in achieving their objective and finishing second in Nations League Group B1, they need to win.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Even then, it might not be enough. Sitting third on seven points going into Monday’s final round of matches, Scotland trail second-placed Slovenia by a point. Should the Slovenians defeat bottom-of-the-table North Macedonia in Skopje, the Scots could win 5-0 and it wouldn’t change the standings.

A draw won’t help either, as Slovenia have a better head-to-head record over Scotland by virtue of their 2-1 win at Hampden last month.

Ending up second is important. It would move Scotland into a play-off spot and a chance of promotion to Nations League A. It would also ensure a second seeding for the Euro 2028 qualification draw next month. Scotland are a host nation for the tournament, and getting in through the back door of a reserved place for non-qualifiers would be embarrassing - although not as humiliating as not being there at all.

The odds of toppling Slovenia, however, are stacked against Scotland. It requires two surprise results. North Macedonia have been meek throughout this campaign and have no points to show for their name, even if their display at Hampden on Friday showed glimmers of improvement in a 2-1 loss. The Scots need a favour in the Balkans.

Switzerland may give Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli some optimism. Yakin is planning to shuffle his pack after landing top spot with a game to spare. Some of the star Swiss names may be kept in reserve. Granit Xhaka, Manuel Akanji, Dan Ndoye and Johan Manzambi are definitely out.

Nevertheless, Yakin vowed that his team will still be strong,. “It has happened a few times already. But we will make sure we get good level of player onto the pitch.

“It’s good thing we have won the group already. It’s now an opportunity to make changes. It doesn’t make sense to wait for injuries players. We have enough opportunities and possibilities.

“We will rotate a but but we first have to make sure that we have a stable defence with experienced defenders. Of course, we will try to get as many players involved as possible. There are a lot of players who haven’t played at all, so they can play from the start.

“We want our boys to get a chance and look forward to it and show their best game. We will certainly make some changes in attack.”

It is of benefit to Scotland that they face an opponent with nothing on the line. Especially as there are areas of concern over how the team has fared so far under Pocognoli’s watch.

The game against Switzerland will be Pocognoli’s sixth in charge after two wins against North Macedonia, two defeats (Switzerland and Slovenia at home) and a draw in Ljubljana. The performance on Friday was far from convincing, but for Pocognoli to get his first win at Hampden should have lifted a bit of weight from the 39-year-old Belgian’s shoulders.

Pocognoli stuck with a back three and Ryan Porteous, Luke Graham and Kieran Tierney coped pretty well with North Macedonia’s blunt attack. The visitors’ goal came from a set-piece and they didn’t look good enough to score in open play, even if they had attacking moments.

The worry for many Scotland fans is that better teams will punish Scotland when they either counter-attack or break through the press. Pocognoli’s insistence on playing a high line and asking his team to be proactive most of the time means that the defence does get exposed. And the top teams will take advantage.

Shorn of many defenders, it is likely Pocognoli will stick with the same back three. There is clamour for a back four, but the head coach will surely be reluctant to throw away all of his work thus far. His biggest conundrum is whether to keep winger Ben Gannon-Doak as his right wing-back or deploy the more rounded and defensively-savvy Aaron Hickey there.

On the other flank, a massive piece of history will be made. Captain Andy Robertson will win his 103rd cap and become Scotland’s most-capped male player of all time. It is an incredible achievement for the 32-year-old, who has been front and centre of Scotland’s recent renaissance and while he will try to shrug off the limelight, this night does belong to him.

Robertson will not want such a milestone tarnished by a defeat and neither will his team-mates. “It just takes time to click but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants,” said striker Che Adams of Pocognoli’s philosophy. “We have been together for a number of years now so we know each other’s game. You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice, we won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

“Coming off a transitional period like we have just now, it’s difficult to know where you are and what you want to do. But all the boys here want to play for our country and do Scotland proud.”

A win in Switzerland would do the nation proud. Depending on what happens 990 miles down the road in Skopje, it may or may not be enough to finish second in the group, but a positive display would give Scotland something to build upon next year when the Euro 2028 qualifiers start and give a sceptical public reasons for optimism.

#1909. De Rossi admits Genoa ‘lost well’ to Milan and recalls Moreira’s comment: “Even our opponents notice”

Daniele De Rossi has looked back at Genoa’s defeat to AC Milan and how he wasn’t frustrated with his team afterwards.

Milan entered the international break with a much-needed victory against Genoa, but it wasn’t the easiest result of the season. After a disappointing defeat to Ferencvaros – which extended the midweek run of defeats – they couldn’t afford to drop points, and they succeeded, even if it wasn’t without flaw.

With two goals inside 20 minutes, you’d be forgiven for expecting Milan to win by more than a couple. However, that was the end of their goalscoring for the afternoon and although Genoa pulled one back, they didn’t grab more than a consolation goal.

Speaking to Sky Sport – in the new series ‘Radici’ – De Rossi looked back on the defeat to the Rossoneri, as well as a comment that stuck with him from Diego Moreira, as MilanPress have relayed today.

We indeed lost against Milan, but we lost ‘well.’ We didn’t deserve it. Three or four weeks ago, the latest results seemed like a pipe dream. I thank the players, staff, and my club for giving me faith and patience at a time when other clubs wouldn’t have had it.

“They remembered how good we did last year. I’m happy to have emerged from a difficult period and to be Genoa’s coach; I’m really happy there.”

“I’m passionate about the fans and the supporters. I’m part of a club that, in terms of fan base, is among the best in Europe. I’m passionate; I don’t punch a clock. I spend two hours with the stockman or the waitress with the same enthusiasm I spend time with the team captain. Experiencing it like that, you realise that Genoa is a great team.

“Genoa is full of Genoese fans who remind you every second how much they love their club, the pride of being the top club in Italy. The architecture of the stadium and the warmth of the fans… I’m not saying this to be a sycophant, but on Sunday Moreira came to me and said, ‘I’ve never seen anything like this here in Italy.’ It’s a reality that even our opponents notice.”
