#1908. I watched Scotland sneak past Wallabies and noted two big replacement plus Rangers stars in stands

Scotland got back on the winning trail with a 15-12 victory over Australia at Murrayfield.

After the disappointment of losing heavily to New Zealand eight days ago, head coach Gregor Townsend will have been pleased to see his team recover - although the triumph was far from swashbuckling.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Mark Atkinson was at Murrayfield to cover proceedings for The Scotsman and picks out some talking points from the match:

Winning was clearly the most important thing for Scotland, which is why with eight minutes to go, Finn Russell took the three points from a penalty rather than going for touch to push for a try.

It moved Scotland ten points clear and left Australia with too much to do, even with Max Jorgensen’s late try to keep the game very close.

However, Scotland’s inability to rack up the points is likely to harm them in the wider scale of the Nations Championship.

With one round of fixtures remaining before finals weekend, Scotland sit fourth in the standings on 15 points with a points difference of -8. After their historic win over New Zealand, fifth-placed Wales also have 15 points but with a points difference of -28. They face Australia next, which is winnable.

Scotland take on whipping boys Japan at Murrayfield on Saturday and need to win comprehensively with a bonus point to put pressure on third-placed Ireland and second-placed England, who are on 20 points and have points differences of +57 and +134 respectively.

Ireland take on South Africa and England face New Zealand, where a solitary bonus point will ensure either of them a top-three finish - and given England’s point difference, it would take something special to overhaul them. Scotland's best hope is probably a big Springbok win.

The chances are Scotland will finish fourth - which would mean a play-off against either Argentina or Australia.

Scotland did not play with much verve or pizzazz and were lamentably wasteful at the start of the second half when Billy Pollard was sent to the sin bin. Rather than adding to the scoreboard, they gave away two cheap penalties and lost their own lineout in a promising position.

Playmaker Russell failed to ignite the game and was patchy with some of his kicking, while the ball very rarely made it out to the wide players.

It wasn’t a game that got the pulses racing and Scotland will likely pay the price.

While both teams will rue not scoring a bucketload of points, there will be some satisfaction from the defensive effort given what happened the previous weekend.

Scotland shipped 43 points to the All Blacks and Australia were on the end of 45 points at Twickenham. It was evident that both sides were intent on keeping the door shut.

While imagination was at a premium, there were a lot of good tackles and discipline when pressure was on. Australia boss Les Kiss referenced it afterwards and Townsend will be pleased with the way his team held firm in difficult conditions for the majority of the final 20 minutes.

Darcy Graham’s tackle right at the end on Tom Wright ensured the win for Scotland and must be applauded for his work at the death.

Scotland had to turn to their bench before and after kick-off, and the replacements did themselves no harm.

Tom Jordan was a last-minute sub for captain Sione Tuipulotu, who failed a late fitness test due to a knee injury. The Bristol Bears man is a versatile fellow and while he’s more often than not been used at 10 or 15 for Scotland, he was asked to partner Huw Jones at centre.

This wasn’t a game for creativity, but Jordan did have some nice offloads and he defended well. If Tuipulotu doesn’t make next week against Japan, Jordan has probably kept himself ahead of Stafford McDowall.

In the pack, Scott Cummings pulled up on 25 minutes and the lock was replaced by his Glasgow Warriors club-mate Max Williamson, who made his presence felt with some big hits and powerful work at the breakdown.

Williamson has found himself behind Cummings and another Glasgow man in Gregor Brown, but this was a performance that will give Townsend food for thought for the rest of the year.

Blair Kinghorn used to be a nailed-on starter for Scotland, but his own form at Toulouse, niggling injuries and the emergence of Kyle Rowe at Glasgow Warriors has put his position in jeopardy.

Townsend gave Kinghorn the whole match at full-back and he served up a reminder of why he can make a difference in the Test arena.

He was secure under the high ball, ran with purpose and broke the line on several occasions. He also put in an excellent tackle on Jorgensen at a crucial point in the game.

Many feel Rowe was unfortunate not to feature against Australia, but Kinghorn has that little bit extra physicality and oomph that sets him apart.

We are also in the midst of an international break in football and that allowed a couple of Rangers players to take in this match.

Scotland striker Lawrence Shankland and Australia midfielder Cammy Devlin are both currently injured, so they were able to watch on in the Murrayfield stands without any commitments - and not far from their old stomping ground.

The ex-Hearts duo seemed to be enjoying the game and Shankland will no doubt have liked Scotland landing the bragging rights over the Wallabies.

Common boss Russ Eldridge said: “I thought the lads were excellent again on Saturday. We've now played two of the best sides in the division in successive weeks and competed really well against both.

“Matt has been outstanding for us recently, but I thought everyone put in a tremendous shift. The second goal came when we were pushing to get something from the game, which was frustrating.

“The performances are certainly improving, and the lads deserve enormous credit for their attitude and commitment. However, we can't keep talking about playing well and coming away with nothing. #1905. Central African Republic vs Benin - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 14 Nov 2026 23:59

Central African Republic host Benin at the Japoma Stadium in Douala, Cameroon, on Monday in the fourth round of Group F in 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

Benin won the first leg 4-1 in Abidjan on Thursday and lead Group F on goal difference, level on seven points with Burkina Faso, while Central African Republic remain bottom with no points and a goal difference of -6.

Central African Republic, known as Les Fauves, have lost all three qualifiers, scoring two goals and conceding eight, and have not won any match since October last year.

Mauritania won 3-1 in their opener on September 24, and Burkina Faso followed with a 1-0 victory over them on September 28.

Head coach Abdelaziz Kerkache, a Moroccan who has previously worked at Mouloudia d’Oujda, was appointed on November 6 to replace Eloge Enza Yamissi, only six days before the first leg.

Kerkache recalled Geoffrey Kondogbia of Olympique de Marseille and Le Mans forward Louis Mafouta, who both missed the opening two qualifiers, and Mafouta responded by equalising in the first leg.

Les Fauves had more of the ball in Abidjan, with 56% possession and eight corners to Benin’s five, yet goalkeeper Dominique Youfeigane faced eight shots on target and conceded four.

Central African Republic are still chasing a first Africa Cup of Nations finals appearance after narrowly missing out in 2021 and 2023, and their home leg is being staged in Douala rather than in Bangui.

Benin, nicknamed Les Guepards, have taken seven points from three Group F games under Gernot Rohr, beginning with a 1-1 draw at Burkina Faso on September 25.

A 2-1 win over Mauritania in Abidjan on September 29 followed, with Rodolfo Aloko scoring either side of half time, as Benin again used an Ivory Coast venue because the Stade de l’Amitie in Cotonou is not yet approved for qualifiers.

Hassane Imourane opened the scoring in the seventh minute of the first leg, Louis Mafouta equalised in the 19th, and Benin were 3-1 up at half time after Aloko struck in the 31st minute and Aiyegun Tosin in the 36th.

Tosin completed his brace in the 56th minute, and he and Aloko have now scored six of Benin’s seven goals in qualifying.

Benin won despite having only 44% of the possession, turning 18 shots into four goals, with eight efforts on target against Central African Republic’s 14 shots and five on target.

Rohr said afterwards that the scoreline flattered his side because Central African Republic attacked a great deal, and he expects a reaction in a rematch only four days later.

For the Central African Republic, Edwin Quarshie, booked in the 1-0 defeat by Burkina Faso, missed the first leg through suspension for accumulated yellow cards and should be available again on Monday.

Venuste Baboula, who has an ankle sprain, was left out of the starting lineup on Thursday, and he could be saved for the return match.

Kondogbia, Mafouta and Goduine Koyalipou all started in Abidjan, and Kerkache has had only one match to work with that group.

For Benin, captain and striker Steve Mounie remains out injured, so Rohr again leans on Aloko, Tosin and Junior Olaitan, who has three goals and seven assists for Besiktas this season.

Parfait Faton, a 16-year-old midfielder from AAS Sarcelles, received his first senior call-up in a 25-player squad that also includes Sessi D’Almeida and Jodel Dossou.

Central African Republic have conceded eight goals in three qualifiers, and a second game in four days under Kerkache is unlikely to repair a defence that let in three before half time on Thursday.

Benin cannot afford to slip either, because Burkina Faso are also on seven points after an added-time winner from Elohim Kabore against Mauritania, and the Cheetahs lead the table only on goal difference.

A clean sheet is less certain, because Mafouta equalised in the first leg and Kondogbia gives Les Fauves a better platform than they had in September, so we expect Central African Republic to score but not to take anything from the game.

The second goal arrived from a free-kick, with the unmarked 6ft 4in Chris Harris directing a header down into Bennett’s path. The Welling midfielder made no mistake, firing a left-footed finish past Roberts to double the advantage.

Things went from bad to worse in the 66th minute when Josh Hallard brought down Anyadike inside the penalty area. The referee pointed to the spot and Bennett calmly converted to complete his hat-trick.

Just five minutes later, Bridges were guilty of another needless foul, as Hayden Neathey brought down Harris. Bennett once again took responsibility from the penalty spot and once again found the net, completing a miserable afternoon for the visitors with his fourth goal of the game.

There was little in the way of a response from Bridges, who offered precious few attacking threats or signs of a fightback. It was another deeply disappointing performance on the road, leaving the travelling supporters with little to take away from yet another unhappy Isthmian League Premier Division away day.

#1903. Celtic treble winner promises to ‘lead change in football’ as he launches bid to overthrow Infantino

Former Celtic defender Ramon Vega has confirmed that he is launching a bid to replace Gianni Infantino as FIFA President at next year’s elections, saying that football must be “for the people, not those who control it.”

Vega, 55, spent a brief but memorable loan spell at Celtic in the second half of the 2000/01 campaign, scoring twice on his debut in a 6-0 win over Aberdeen. He also had spells at Tottenham Hotspur and Cagliari during his 13-year career, and earned 23 caps for Switzerland.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

During his six-month loan stint at Celtic Park, Vega quickly developed into a fan favourite as part of a Martin O'Neill side that lifted a domestic treble in 2001. However, his stay in Glasgow was brief, and he signed for Watford on a free transfer shortly afterwards, after the London club offered him the security of a longer contract at Vicarage Road.

Retiring two years later, he has forged a successful career in global finance and asset management, but Vega now believes the time is right to oust under-pressure President Infantino when the elections formally take place at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco next March.

The Swiss defender, who can speak six languages, has ran for the role three times previously, in 2015, 2019 and 2023, but maintains his belief that he can succeed in his bid to become the next FIFA President, stating that “football stands at a defining crossroads” and that “the decisions we make today will shape the future of our beautiful game for generations to come.”

Writing on his official X (formerly Twitter) account, he said on Sunday: “A credible FIFA begins with a credible election. UEFA provided Infantino with €500,000 in official campaign funding to support his global travel and logistics ahead of the February 2016 FIFA Extraordinary Congress. Europe played a decisive role in bringing the current leadership to FIFA therefore also has a huge responsibility to help bring about change.

“I call for open and transparent dialogue across the entire global football family. Major decisions affecting our game should never be imposed. They must follow genuine consultation, where every voice is heard and the broadest possible consensus is built before decisions are made. The solution is a credible candidate, a democratic election, a clear program capable of restoring trust, integrity, transparency and unity.

“I offer every member association a neutral, independent and credible democratic alternative, a candidate rooted in the game, who can bridge football and international finance &business, bring cultures together and lead FIFA with competence, integrity and independence. For me serving football is not about personal ambition. It's a responsibility, a duty and a matter of honour.”

To officially run for the Presidency, the former Celtic man must win the backing of five or more national federations before Wednesday’s [November 18] deadline. However, this could be possible, with Vega claiming he has backing across every continent, though he has yet to reveal who is endorsing him.

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin breathed a sigh of relief after seeing the penalty he conceded just minutes after his introduction to the pitch saved by Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens during Belgium’s thumping 4-1 win over Italy in the Nations League on Sunday night.

Despite starting Belgium’s 2-1 win away over Turkiye on Thursday night, the Rangers star had to be content with a place on the bench against Italy as Mark van Bommel’s side looked to seal a place in the quarter-finals of the Nations League at the Stade Roi Baudouin.

Two points ahead of their visitors ahead of the Group A1 clash on nine points, the game got off to a disastrous start for the hosts when Italy went into an 11th-minute lead when Brentford defender Michael Kayode's cross to Pio Esposito to score 10th international goal in 15 appearances.

However, the lead was short-lived, and Belgium found themselves back on level terms just four minutes later when Brighton wing-back Maxim de Cuyper slammed home to restore parity in Brussels, before centre-back Nathan Ngoy rifled home from close range after a scramble in the box on 22 minutes.

Jeremy Doku then completed the turnaround when he added a third for Belgium just four minutes later, dancing through the Italian defence with stunning footwork before firing a low drive beyond his Manchester City teammate Gianluigi Donnarumma in the visitor’s goal. Despite the Group standings being all but confirmed, the action did not cease, with Italy awarded a last-minute penalty after VAR ruled that Raskin had handled Alphadjo Cisse’s shot in the area. The Rangers man had replaced Romeo Lavia just over 10 minutes earlier, but needn’t have worried, as goalkeeper Lammens pulled off an excellent save to deny Esposito a brace.

“If Donnarumma had not been in goal, then we would've scored six,” said new Belgium head coach van Bommel. “I'll be honest, I didn't expect this when we started two months ago, but even before that first match with Italy, I could tell this was a really intelligent group of players. That makes it a pleasure for a coach to work with them.

“These players can anticipate an opponent, are flexible, and can adapt to different situations. Today you saw that reflected. Not only was the idea right, individually many players stepped up too. And ultimately we managed to dominate an opponent like Italy for long periods. That is the most important thing to me."

Belgium will discover their Nations League quarter-final opponents on Friday, November 20, 2026, with the draw set to take place at 11am UK time in Nyon, Switzerland.

#1898. GdS: Linear structure and a strong work force – what Krösche is likely to implement at Milan

AC Milan are expected to hire Markus Krösche in the next few weeks, and a report has looked a little more at his work today.

Between Eintracht Frankfurt and Milan, there are plenty of differences. From the finances available to how they’re spent, even to the way in which the structure of the club ticks over. So, Krösche will have to learn with the Rossoneri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it won’t be a one way street, with the Diavolo needing to learn plenty too.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, Krösche methods are very linear; it’s about arriving and leaving at the right time, having the knowledge to enter and the courage to step away when the time is right.

His belief is that the club will always hold more weight than the manager, which has been shown in the past few months by Gerry Cardinale and there is no shortage of exciting signings on his CV.

What is also worth remembering is that he’s not one to step away from his methods. In 2022, he was given a chance to sign Cristiano Ronaldo. However, it didn’t make sense for him or Frankfurt, so they never made their move.

If it happens his way, Timmo Hardung will arrive alongside the German. The pair met at RB Leipzig and their relationship has only grown since then and Krösche eventually led a team of 70 people at Frankfurt. In other words, he won’t be out of place at the top of the Milan football organisation.

Gazzetta even suggests that it’s ‘no secret’ that his desire is to move to Italy to work under Krösche once again. Given their successes together, it makes sense why all parties are hoping to keep that relationship under the same roof.

#1895. Iceland vs Luxembourg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 15 Nov 2026 00:03, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 03:16

Iceland will look to wrap up automatic promotion when they welcome Luxembourg to Reykjavik for Monday's Nations League encounter.

The hosts are sitting two points at the top of Group C4, while the visitors are languishing at the bottom of the standings ahead of the final matchday of the league phase.

After being relegated from League B in 2024-25, Iceland have put in a strong performance in their first-ever League C campaign, collecting 11 points from a possible 15.

After playing out a 1-1 draw with Estonia, Arnar Gunnlaugsson's side recorded back-to-back 3-0 victories over Luxembourg and Bulgaria.

However, their momentum was somewhat halted by a goalless draw against Estonia in their final outing of the September/October international break.

But they certainly had no issues troubling the scorers in Friday's emphatic 5-0 away win over Iceland, which came courtesy of an Andri Gudjohnsen hat-trick, an Orri Oskarsson effort and an own goal.

Gudjohnsen, who is now the leading scorer in League C with five goals, has helped his country secure a playoff berth and put them in pole position to secure automatic promotion on the final matchday.

With a two-point advantage over Estonia, Iceland know a win would guarantee a first-place finish, while a draw would likely be enough due to their significant goal difference advantage.

They would even progress with a defeat if Estonia fail to beat Bulgaria, but they will certainly fancy their chances of taking all three points, considering they are currently League C's highest scorers and have recorded shutouts in each of their last five matches.

Luxembourg are competing in their fourth consecutive League C campaign, knowing they will remain in the third tier no matter the result in Monday's trip to the Icelandic capital.

That is because they are six points adrift of the top two after each of their last four matches since beating Bulgaria 2-1 on matchday one.

In fact, they have failed to trouble the scorers in each of those four defeats, including another goal-shy display in Friday's narrow 1-0 home loss against Estonia, leaving them one point behind third-placed Bulgaria.

That result made it three consecutive home losses without troubling the scorers since Luxembourg won 3-0 against Malta in the second leg of their Nations League relegation/promotion playoff tie in March.

As they head on their travels for Monday's fixture, Jeff Strasser's side can take confidence from the fact they have won three of their last four away internationals, although their most recent away outing resulted in a 1-0 defeat against Estonia.

If they were to win on Monday, it would represent their first-ever away victory over Iceland and just their second head-to-head success at any venue after winning 3-1 in a European Championship qualifier in September 2023.

Iceland will be unable to call upon Stefan Teitur Thordarson and Kristall Mani Ingason, who were forced in the first half against Bulgaria.

Hordur Magnusson replaced Thordarson in the ninth minute in Plovdiv, but he will miss Monday’s fixture through suspension after picking up his second yellow card of the league phase.

As a result of those absences, Gunnlaugsson has decided to call up Hjortur Hermannsson, Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Saevar Atli Magnusson.

As for the visitors, Omar Natami will serve a one-match ban after collecting his second yellow card of the league phase in the narrow loss to Estonia.

In positive news, Dirk Carlson is back from suspension and is expected to slot into central defence for Monday’s away fixture.

Enes Mahmutovic and Enzo dos Santos are also pushing for starting spots after coming off the bench to play over 30 minutes in Friday’s defeat.

Valdimarsson; Palsson, Gunnarsson, Gretarsson, Tomasson; Ellertsson, Johannesson, Haraldsson, Sigurdsson; Oskarsson, Gudjohnsen

Moris; Bohnert, Selimovic, Mahmutovic, Carlson; Olesen; V Thill, Dos Santos, Cruz, Kadamani; Dardari

Iceland will be full of confidence after thrashing Bulgaria 5-0 last time out, and we think they will produce another free-scoring display against a Luxembourg side that are low on confidence after four consecutive defeats.

With the game entering the final stages, Rangers forward Naderi was introduced in the 74th minute as a substitute for Christophe Kabongo, and he helped Czechia level the score shortly afterwards.

Scoring nine goals and assisting five more for Rangers this season, he was on the field just 10 minutes before he found strike partner Adam Hlozek in a dangerous scoring position. His initial effort was blocked, but Hlozek reacted quickest to rifle home a left-footed finish to level the level. However, just as it appeared that Naderi’s had helped his side steal a late point, Croatia restored their lead three minutes later through substitute Lovro Majer.

Taking a pass from Brighton centre-back Luka Vuskovic in the away side’s area, he drilled a low drive into the net to condemn Czechia to a seventh consecutive defeat and the worst losing streak in their history.

Beginning in the group stages of this summer’s World Cup in North America, Czechia’s slide began with a 3-0 defeat to Mexico and has carried straight through into a brutal Nations League campaign against Spain, England, and Croatia.

The group stage of the Nations League is almost at a close, with the final fixtures taking place this week across Europe.

Won by Portugal last year, they claimed a second title with a penalty shootout win over Spain after playing out a thrilling 2-2 draw with Spain in Munich, Germany. Winners of the inaugural tournament in 2019, they are now the most successful team in Nations League history, ahead of Spain and France, who have one win each.

Want to know when the draw for the Nations League quarter-final takes place, who has qualified and when the games will take place? Here’s everything you need to know:

Get our daily football newsletter by clicking here.

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals will take place on Friday, 20 November. The draw begins at 11am UK time and will take place at UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

As of November 15, the following teams have confirmed a place in the Nations League quarter-finals: France, Belgium, England, Portugal and Spain.

In total, eight teams qualify for the quarter-finals via League A. The four League A group winners are seeded and placed in Pot 1 of the draw, with the four League A group runners-up are placed in Pot 2 and unseeded. Each group winner is drawn against a runner-up from a different group. Teams from the same group cannot play each other in the quarter-finals.

Teams placed in Leagues B, C and D all compete for promotion and relegation, and are unable to qualify for the knockout stage of the competition.

The upcoming quarter-final ties will be played over two legs during the March 2027 international break. The seeded group winners will play the first leg away from home, with the second leg on home soil. First legs are scheduled to take place from 25–27 March 2027, and second legs follow from 28–30 March 2027.

The draw will not be broadcast in the UK and Ireland. However, they are several options to stream the draw live, which are detailed below.

If you want to stream the draw via your smart TV, laptop, tablet or mobile phone, the entire ceremony will be streamed for free via UEFA.tv and via the official UEFA YouTube channel.

#1890. Wilson’s wondrous finish seals FA Trophy win as Eastbourne Borough close door on Curfews

Tyano Wilson, just 18, had been pitched into the action by manager Steve King on 74 minutes in a last attempt to break the deadlock ahead of a potential penalty shoot-out – and the young man seized his opportunity.

A pass into his feet, just inside the box. A touch, a swerve to the left, and just enough space and sight of goal. A fizzing left-foot shot that found the top corner with Chertsey keeper Luke Roberts clutching at thin air: 2-1 and the Sports had claimed a memorable victory.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It had been a cracking contest, and the visitors had played a full part. Borough had slightly more of the ball and slightly the better chances, but after claiming a ludicrously early lead, they never put the game to bed – and a fateful red card, late in the first half, had put the home side at a disadvantage for an hour.

What a start for the Sports. After successfully defending two Chertsey corners in the first two minutes, the home side broke with Josh Rees through the right channel and Terrell Egbri blitzed down the touchline. He raced on to the pass, a touch, a delightful looped cross just too high for startled keeper Roberts, and there at the back post was Paul McCallum to head home.

But the Curfews – among the leaders in their own Southern Premier division – had not come south for a charabanc outing, and they responded strongly. Liam Nash saw his 25-yarder spilled for a Borough corner – from which Chertsey raced the length of the pitch and almost equalised.

The high pace was matched by some physical moments, too. Chertsey had copped one early yellow card, but they escaped sanctions for a couple of heavy challenges, a blatant handball and an obvious trip on Liam Nash in the area.

On the other hand, Freddie Carter was fortunate to escape without a card for one pretty blatant challenge on Nathan Minhas 20 minutes, and these marginal moments tend to even out. Chances were being traded like swap cards.

Then, a potentially game-changing moment. After an apparent elbow in Egbri’s face had been unpunished, Borough left-back Nathan Laleye did incur the ultimate sanction four minutes before half-time: a little wrestle with Chertsey danger man Minhas was judged a denial of a scoring opportunity – and Mr Black flourished red.

Arguably Carter – spared his own red card earlier – was in a covering position, but referees do not have multi-angle replays, and the Sports would have to play for almost an hour a man down. King responded at once by replacing Darren McQueen with full-back Elliott Johnson.

Alex Fisher, on a yellow card, escaped a second caution after first fouling Egbri and then kicking the ball away.

After half-time, Chertsey were on the front foot at once. Minhas put one effort too high and a second chance wide, but Borough were feeling anything but comfortable. The minutes were clicking away, painfully slowly for home supporters but a little anxiously for the Curfews – until exactly at the mid-point of the second half, the visitors had their chance.

Harry Phipps, working overtime at the heart of defence, tripped Leo Farruch, who had just spurned a priceless chance. A clear penalty, and Minhas seized the chance to equalise from the spot.

One-all, and as the Curfews pressed their one-man advantage, the Sports were digging deep. Their best chance seemed to be the penalty shoot-out – or could the ten men somehow snatch a winner?

Veteran semi-pros only grit their teeth and and resign themselves. But buoyant 18-year-olds, unleashed off the bench, seize the moment.

And Wilson, in those final 15 minutes, would claim the moment. Into added time, he took possession a yard inside the Chertsey area, shimmied left to open up a sight of goal, and smashed a dream of a shot into the top right corner. Despair for the Curfews, elation for the Sports.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest. The 30-year-old striker was taken to hospital where he died the following morning.

The Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has now issued the maximum suspension possible for Owono’s challenge.

A statement said: ‘The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.’

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono insisted he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

‘We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.’

Earlier this week, Spanish newspaper Marca reported that Owono is barely leaving his house following De Miguel’s death and is closely working with psychologists and doctors.

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has defended his choice to remain at Manchester City amid the fallout of their guilty verdict.

Things aren’t going so well for City in the league but we’ll try and turn that around against Fulham."

Haaland signed a new contract until 2034 in January 2025, though it is not clear if he would seek a move away from the club should they be severely punished.

City could win an appeal later this year, but the likelihood of the club overturning their guilty verdict is reportedly small.

A demotion to the Championship or lower divisions raises the possibility of a mass exodus, especially if the players have clauses in their contracts that make exits easier in the event of relegation.

Haaland is arguably the best striker in the world, and the 26-year-old will not want to spend at least a year of his prime competing for promotion.

It would not be surprising if the likes of Phil Foden or Nico O'Reilly opted to stay at the Etihad given they came through the academy, but it is hard to see others such as Haaland remaining a City player.

These lot will give you a chance is the sentence that every opposing League One manager must surely utter when talk turns to Barnsley.

You don't have to play particularly well to beat them and that is a considerable worry.

They have been in most games this season, but eventually err.

Concentration, physicality and sensing danger are all areas where this group are deficient. A disturbing cocktail. They don’t handle pressure, quite simply and their game management is lamentable.

Barnsley have lost their last five away league matches. Their concession of 17 goals in the second half of games is the joint-worst record in the third tier.

The 23rd-placed Reds, only kept off the bottom by goal difference, are winless in nine league matches since September 2. Autumn, certainly on the league front, has been appalling.

Ahead of kick-off, the Monkees "I’m a Believer" got an airing on the Wigan jukebox. Bob Marley’s classic “Three Little Birds” - a song beloved of Barnsley - did the rounds at the final whistle as Wigan escaped the relegation zone after showing the savvy.

Barnsley should be worried about a number of things, for sure.

As is their manager. Keep the Faith is the motto of the Northern Soul movement - another thing associated with Wigan.

Daniel Stendel was clearly struggling on that count in the immediate aftermath of events on Saturday.

He spoke about holding discussions with Reds majority shareholder/chairman Neerav Parekh. Not necessarily about his own position - not yet, anyway - but endeavouring to find ways to support a playing squad who plainly need help.

It was all a bit unclear. It wasn't to do with bringing in more free agents either.

Then what was it? Discussing what Barnsley need to do in the January transfer window should be top of the agenda. Even if it feels some way in the distance.

Make no mistake, if the Oakwell outfit get the winter window wrong, then there is a pretty high chance that they will be playing fourth-tier football next season for the first time since 1978-79 unfortunately.

A relatively even first half had one key moment.

Fraser Murray had delivered a warning with his sweet curler producing a full-stretch parry from Ceiran Slicker.

A few minutes later, the Reds custodian had no chance when Murray again showed delicious technique to bend an unstoppable low shot into the far corner, for his first goal of the campaign. An important one.

How the ball arrived at his feet, with Wigan afforded an ocean of space in the middle of the pitch was poor from a Reds perspective. Latics also fancied it out wide against both Ziyad Larkeche and Jubril Okedina.

On the resumption, Barnsley found a much-needed lifeline in front of their admirable band of stoic supporters. Luca Connell found Reyes Cleary - who worried Wigan for most of the afternoon.

He expertly manufactured space before fizzing over a superb low cross which was buried by Cam McGeehan, backing up in the box.

It was classic wing-play from Cleary to present an opportunity on a plate for McGeehan, who struck his ninth goal of the campaign.

Barnsley had their tails up, but - all the while - there was a nagging feeling about what might happen at the other end. The fears were borne out in appalling fashion.

Morgan Fox hung up a cross which was attacked by Jensen Weir. Larkeche, having a poor game, challenged meekly and Weir couldn’t believe his luck.

His header caught Slicker by surprise at the near post as he could only pat the effort into the net, horribly. And that was that. A scruffy concession in a bedraggled season. Sheffield Wednesday next.

Wigan Athletic: Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett (Trevitt 68), Weir, Power, Mellish; Burrowes (Miller 87), Murray; Saydee (Hogan 67). Substitutes unused: J Walsh, Chilokoa-Mullen, A Harris, Higgins.

#1880. Di'Shon Bernard goal points to Sheffield Wednesday tweak that can up entertainment levels

Despite the 3-0 scoreline over Plymouth Argyle, Challinor's first league game as Owls manager only really delivered on the first front.

But it would be unreasonable to expect an instant transformation, especially with injuries forcing players into unfamiliar positions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After six games without a win and cup defeats in Challinor's first two matches, Wednesday just needed to get over the line.

But on an afternoon where the football never rivalled Plymouth's orange away kit for brightness, one moment really stood out.

It was born of a mistake, Di'Shon Bernard failing to find Keillor-Dunn after winning the ball deep in Wednesday territory.

But when Malachi Boateng's interception turned into a one-two and the centre-back drove into shooting range and scored in off a post.

The game already won by Keillor-Dunn's finish two minutes earlier, it was no more than the cherry on the cake, six games into Bernard’s return from a 19-month knee injury.

But the story of Henrik Pedersen's tenure was clear – excited by the potential of David Storch’s ownership, Owls fans are greedy. They do not just want the cake, they want the cherries too. After the thin gruel of last season, who can blame them?

"I want people to be brave," said Challinor. "If the shot goes into the Kop, so be it. I'll always encourage people to make positive decisions.

"They're going to make mistakes. We're going to ask them to do things that are different.

"Of course we'll get frustrated, but that's acceptable. That's on us and that will always be the case."

Wednesday's shape flitted between a 4-2-3-1 and a 3-2-4-1 when Sil Swinkels tucked from left-back into a more familiar position.

Back threes need a player willing to break out, especially on days – not Saturday, in fairness – when the visitors come to S6 to frustrate.

"We should, if we do things right, come up against more blocks and teams getting men behind the ball,” argued Challinor.

"That's when people need to step in, be positive and make the most of opportunities. That comes from backing yourself, and quality."

Bernard, a team-mate of Marcus Rashford in the Manchester United youth ranks, has that.

"He wants to put his body on the line," commented Challinor. "He got injured at Notts County by blocking a shot and opening his knee up.

"There's loads of work we can do with him, he can get so much better.

"We'll ask him to be better and more positive in possession as well as being able to do the other things."

When pressed into giving the ball up in the 37th minute he got back to kill the move when it came into the penalty area. When Xavier Amaechi threatened to force his way through, Bernard refused to be shaken off and made an excellent recovery tackle.

He believes working with Challinor and his assistant Clint Hill – more no-nonsense centre-backs in their day – can elevate his game.

"Playing the right of a three he's trusting me to do more on the ball," he says. "Before I got injured, that was probably one of my strengths.

"Now I need to really just build up the confidence to do more of it because you can see in glimpses I am capable of it.

"He's pushing me to be that player and I'm grateful him and his staff have shown that's what I need to do."

For the 80 minutes before those two goals in two minutes there was not a great deal to write home about.

The fizzing atmosphere Challinor was looking forward to after only tasting Hillsborough-lite in the EFL Trophy was flat for an hour because Wednesday's football was.

Although they were fortunate Roman Curtis' chest high tackle on Jamal Lowe only got a yellow card, Plymouth should have gone in at half-time multiple goals up.

Instead, when Bernard's goalbound header was nodded over at the end of the first half, Billy Mitchell’s deflected shot from the corner brought his first goal since 2021.

The second half was more even but Hillsborough helped its team over the line.

Having missed an easy chance from a quick throw-in, Keillor-Dunn poked home the loose ball at a badly-defended free-kick and at 2-0 the contest was over.

But the mouth-watering bit was still to come.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Mitchell, Heskey; Slattery, Bannan (Barry 72), J Lowe (Palmer 85); Keillor-Dunn (Gray 85).

Unused substitutes: Santos, Trueman, Weaver, Thornton.

Plymouth Argyle: Cooper; Harding, MacKenzie (Irow 63), Hartridge; Curtis, Boateng, White (Oseni 77), Ross; Amaechi, Ibrahim (Watts 63); Evans.

Unused substitutes: Storer, Campbell, Mwaro, Maund.

​The misses: Plymouth spurned some great chances, Xavier Amaechi horribly failing to make contact with a ball in from Bradley Ibrahim, then heading a great second-half chance from a Alex Hartridge cross wide. Earlier, Will Evans cushioned a volley into the side netting when Joe Lumley’s flapping at a corner left the goal gaping.

Star performers: Di’Shon Bernard was excellent but so too was midfielder Billy Mitchell, the stand-out Owls player in a first half where they were well below par.

Run over: This was the first time in eight league games Hillsborough’s attendance had officially fallen below 30,000 – though only by 772. The football did not lift them in the first half but they took it upon themselves to inspire the players around the hour.

#1879. Moretto provides update on Milan’s Endrick and Tresoldi pursuits: “Really likes him”

In January, AC Milan will make some big investments, if reports are to be believed. Currently, two names are leading the talk.

It could be a big month for Milan if things go their way in January. They hope to add a central defender to their squad – and have hoped to do so since before the end of the summer mercato – but the headline signing may be an attacking option, with quite a few names in the mix.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The favourites are clear, though: Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi.

Speaking on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Matteo Moretto provided an update on the Rossoneri’s pursuit for both forwards and whether either was progressing, as MilanNews relayed.

“Although Mourinho continues to say that Endrick will stay at Real Madrid, the truth is that the player has the ball right now. If the player decides to tell Real Madrid that he wants to try a new experience to grow and play, Real Madrid will not object. And I can tell you that these are precisely the indications.

“To date, there have been no official communications between the parties, but I can confirm that Endrick, as he also stated in a recent interview, is open to a new loan experience, Lyon-style, which could give him that extra focus and playing time, also with a view to the national team.

“A few days ago, I told you how Milan were really close to signing Tresoldi a few years ago, so much so that the player arrived, visited Milanello, and stayed at Casa Milan; the contracts were even ready.

“I want to clarify that, since he was a very young player at the time, it wasn’t a deal directly supervised by Paolo Maldini. There were other people managing the deal. Ricky Massara was also Milan’s transfer manager at the time, and there were others as well.

“The deal never actually got signed because Milan stalled, and the player returned to Germany, effectively signing a new contract with Hannover. Beyond that, there’s a lot of talk about Tresoldi now in terms of Milan’s present and future.

“I want to clarify a few points, however. I can confirm that it’s true that Cardinale really likes him, and Milan really likes him. The club is evaluating what steps to take to make this kind of move…”

It’s clear that the Diavolo are keen to add some attacking firepower to their ranks in January, understandably. However, it must be the right fit and there are certainly a few questions about Tresoldi now, with the price only rising.

#1877. Greece vs Serbia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 02:13, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 05:04

Under pressure in League A of the UEFA Nations League, Greece will welcome Serbia to Panthessaliko Stadium for their final Group A2 showdown on Monday.

The Azure and White are battling for a place in the quarter-finals, while the Eagles are competing to earn a place in the League A/B playoffs.

Ivan Jovanovic's Greece kicked off their Nations League campaign in excellent fashion, but have been on a slow descent as the group has progressed.

The Azure and White beat Monday's opponents 2-1 in their opener on September 24, before claiming an impressive 1-0 victory over Germany three days later.

However, that success in Augsburg was Jovanovic's side's last taste of triumph, even if following it up with a pair of home draws against the Netherlands and Die Mannschaft was commendable.

On Friday, Greece were thrashed 7-0 by Xavi's Oranje, a defeat that was not only humiliating but has put their path to the quarter-finals in jeopardy.

Monday's hosts are currently second in Group A2, level on eight points with Germany, and must match their result while hoping Jurgen Klopp's team drop points on home soil in order to finish in the top two.

Meanwhile, Veljko Paunovic's Serbia have endured a disastrous Nations League term and are now fighting to avoid automatic demotion to League B, the fate awaiting the two lowest-ranked fourth-placed teams in League A.

The Eagles have lost all five of their matches so far, and are doomed to finish bottom of the group as a result, but they can still make the playoffs if they can rank higher than Turkey from Group A1 and the Czech Republic or Croatia from Group A3.

Paunovic's side are currently level on zero points with both Turkey and the Czech Republic, while boasting a three-superior goal-difference to those nations and a four-goal advantage over Croatia, who have three points.

Fans looking for a reason to be hopeful ahead of Monday's showdown could lean on the fact that Serbia were able to score in four of their defeats, three of which were by just one goal.

On the other hand, the Eagles were beaten 3-1 by Germany on Friday, falling two goals behind with just 14 minutes on the clock before having two players sent off in the second half.

That latest disappointment means the visitors have conceded 11 times in just five games - a rate of 2.2 per match - and their leaky defence could be exploited by a motivated Greece.

Greece are expected to be without midfielder Dimitrios Kourbelis due to an ankle injury, though Nectarios Triantis and Athanasios Androutsos should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

Out wide, Arsenal's Christos Tzolis and Borussia Dortmund starboy Konstantinos Karetsas will be hoping to support a strike partnership of Vangelis Pavlidis and Fotis Ioannidis up top.

As for Serbia, they are missing Rangers midfielder Vanja Dragojevic and PAOK winger Andrija Zivkovic, both of whom are suspended after being sent off against Germany.

Filling the gaps, manager Paunovic could opt for Stefan Dzodic to be joined by Lazar Samardzic and Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in midfield.

Further forward, Mihajlo Cvetkovic is likely to partner captain and record appearance holder Dusan Tadic in attack, desperate to fire his team into the playoffs.

Tzolakis; Rota, Mavropanos, Retsos, Tsimikas; Karetsas, Triantis, Androutsos, Tzolis; Pavlidis, Ioannidis

V Milinkovic-Savic; Nedeljkovic, Gudelj, Milenkovic, Babic, Sukacev; Samardzic, Dzodic, S Milinkovic-Savic; Cvetkovic, Tadic

Greece may have been hammered 7-0 by the Netherlands last time out, but that defeat came as a shock, and with a place in the quarter-finals at stake, the hosts will be motivated to bounce back.

Serbia have struggled throughout this term's Nations League, and it would be surprising to see them avoid a sixth consecutive defeat on Monday.

#1876. Sheffield Wednesday's Dave Challinor on his summer set-piece education at Brentford

During his time out of work at the start of this season, Challinor visited the training grounds of Celtic, West Bromwich Albion and Brentford amongst others to broaden his horizons.

And the effect of his trip to see the Bees was evident on Saturday as the Owls registered their first win under him courtesy of two goals from set pieces to beat Plymouth Argyle.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Billy Mitchell opened the scoring with a shot which took a massive deflection at a 45th-minute corner. It was the midfielder's first goal since 2021.

Davis Keillor-Dunn then scored his sixth goal in nine matches when the Pilgrims failed to deal with a Callum Slattery free-kick.

Centre-back Di'Shon Bernard completed the scoring with a brilliant individual effort.

"I went to Brentford in the summer for a few days and saw how seriously they take it," said Challinor of set-pieces.

"They have set-pieces as part of every single training session for them, whether it's warm-ups or practise, delivery, finishing will be important. It's something that we are really keen to make sure we do practise and we do work at.

"It's not the most exciting thing in the world is it, practising set-piece delivery, but if you get the reinforcement on a Saturday it makes it a whole lot easier.

"We are really conscious and want to make sure the record we have is a positive one and Saturday helps.

"Keith (Andrews, Brentford's coach) was really helpful in me going up there so I spent a few days with them.

"It's an amazing environment, I learnt so much. There will be things from there that we'd love to incorporate here.

"It's a brilliantly run football club that have the success based on consistency right from the very top."

Wednesday's win, their first in seven matches in all competitions, took them above Tom Cleverley's Plymouth and back into the League One play-off places.

The result, it must be said, was better than the performance, and Challinor was not getting carried away at the end of his first league game as Owls manager, after consecutive cup defeats to begin his reign.

"I think we've got loads to do,” he said. “(At half-time) I was really open with the players and asked them what they thought. Sometimes it takes 10 minutes to earn the right (to play), sometimes it takes 60 minutes, sometimes you never earn the right.

"Plymouth are really good at asking questions of you, and in the first half I don't think we dealt with them questions well enough at times.

"We maybe needed to compete better and win first contacts and drop on second balls and track runners. We probably got away with it a little bit at times.

"But they were really honest about that and said that was the case.

"The second half was much, much better. I thought we dealt with their threats and then we were able to make the game look a little bit more like we'd want it to look like."

"The one and only thing we can do is stand up. The derby is a big game, not only in our situation, but also for the club and for the supporters. It's a big opportunity for us to give a little bit back from what we got from our supporters."

Top-scorer and captain Cameron McGeehan picked up his fifth league booking of the campaign at the Brick Community Stadium.

#1872. Manchester United: Sir Alex Ferguson has already approved of Mauricio Pochettino as talks planned

Mauricio Pochettino says he will have the opportunity to speak to Sir Alex Ferguson as his Manchester United tenure gets underway.

Pochettino was announced as the new Man United head coach on Friday, succeeding Michael Carrick who had been sacked the day before, with the club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

However, the Argentine has not yet officially started work at Old Trafford.

As communicated in Man Utd’s official statement, Pochettino has been allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) and their double-header against Haiti.

The first of which took place on Saturday evening with USA recording a 6-0 win to put one foot in the CONCACAF Nations League finals.

Following Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge of USA, he spoke to the Telegraph and was asked if he can spoken to Ferguson since accepting the Man United job.

“Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,” the 54-year-old said.

“I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

“For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense. But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.”

Pochettino and Ferguson have remained in close contact since first dining with each other in 2016.

They first crossed paths in the dugout during the 2012-13 season when Man United beat Southampton at Old Trafford, though Pochettino left a lasting impression on Ferguson despite the defeat.

"For the first 30 minutes we were fantastic," Ferguson told BBC Sport in January 2013. "But in the second half Southampton have been the best team to play here this season. We were fortunate to win."

Then in 2016, David Lammy, MP for Tottenham, shared details of a meeting with Ferguson at a charity function.

"I’m going to let you in to a secret," Lammy told The Spurs Show podcast. "About six weeks ago I sat next to Alex Ferguson at a dinner in support of grassroots football abroad.

"He said to me, 'I think you guys have the best manager in the Premier League.' Alex Ferguson said that."

#1871. How Harrogate Town banished ghosts of Carlisle United with 4-0 rout of Altrincham - analysis

When Altrincham defender Reuben Lopata-White lunged in on Harrogate Town winger Ellis Taylor, there will have been two shivers down the spines of the home supporters.

The first one being the natural one, brought on by the reckless nature of the loaned-out Leeds United prospect’s foul. The second will have been prompted by the dawning realisation of what comes next.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Harrogate have not had the best of times against 10-man sides and lost 3-0 to a Carlisle United side who saw two men sent off less than three weeks ago.

Halloween has been and gone, but the ghosts of Carlisle threatened to haunt when the red card was brandished on the 13-minute mark.

“I think everyone in the stadium thought that [it was going to be a struggle],” said Harrogate boss Simon Weaver. “[Altrincham] probably, ultimately, were buoyed by the fact that it didn't go our way the last time.

“It's not a case of sulking and berating everyone when it just didn't work on that occasion, but are we capable of next time, especially against a really good team like Altrincham, carrying out our roles a bit better?”

To say Harrogate carried out their roles a bit better would be an understatement. The strong Sulphurite grip on the game rarely loosened as they cruised to an emphatic 4-0 win.

It took until the second half but once the hosts started firing on all cylinders in the final third, the afternoon raced away from the Robins.

Will McGowan drew first blood shortly after the restart and Morgan Williams pounced merely 10 minutes later.

Pressure continued to be applied and the advantage was built upon by Michael Craig and Rohan Vaughan, who both hammered home thunderous strikes.

Ellis Taylor may not have etched his name on the scoresheet but the Marcy Fitness Stadium became his playground, one in which he toyed with defenders with relative ease.

“We still had to be very patient,” said Weaver. “[We had] to really break through and put the game to bed.

“We did in the end and that's what mattered and a growing maturity I thought the lads showed today.

“You’ve got to kill off the hope, kill off the energy and psychologically I think the best way of doing it is to keep the ball and keep probing and not get flustered ourselves.”

Boreham Wood have steamed away at the top of the National League table but it remains early days. Harrogate reduced the gap between the sides to 10 points and will be keen to keep chipping away.

As for the ghosts of Carlisle - consider them banished.

“I think we've got a really good, honest group,” said Weaver. “There’s blips on the journey of every team but 18 new players and people are handling disappointments well, people aren't getting over the top or egotistical when we bang a few goals in.

“They want to play and they want to play in the right way but not play boring football. We’ve got a proud record at home.”

#1870. Erling Haaland speaks out on Manchester City future as financial scandal rumbles on

Erling Haaland says he knows little or nothing about the financial scandal Manchester City are involved and is happy at the club, having signed a contract running until 2034.

In September Manchester City were found guilty of over 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City were found to have artificially inflated their financial position by over £900 million from 2009-18.

The club is now appealing those guilty verdict, with a hearing taking place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

If the appeal is unsuccessful than punishment is likely to be severe, with points deductions and fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League a possibility.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Manchester City’s players have not said much about the situation and continue to compete, although three league defeats on the spin to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest may suggest the situation is taking its toll.

Haaland, though, says he has not even looked into the scandal much, pointing out that he was not at the club during the period of time that has been under investigation.

The 26-year-old scored in Norway’s 3-1 win over Wales on Saturday in Oslo and after successfully converting from the penalty spot, he successfully dodged the issue while speaking to TV2.

‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he said. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’

The iconic striker then joked that these questions should be put to his compatriots that were at Manchester City during the time period in question.

Haaland dug out some names that only die hard Manchester City fans wil remember, saying: ‘There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think.

‘Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can’t remember.

‘But it’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come… I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

‘To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything.’

Haaland stuck to his guns when asked about his thoughts on his future amid the ongoing appeal process.

‘I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,’ he said. ‘I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

‘I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

‘Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.’

#1869. Arsenal: Viktor Gyokeres overtakes Cristiano Ronaldo, extends all-time Nations League goals record

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 07:35

Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres extended an extraordinary UEFA Nations League goals record and surpassed Cristiano Ronaldo in Sweden's 3-2 victory over Bosnia-Herzegovina on Saturday evening.

The 28-year-old has experienced a frustrating start to the 2026-27 season with Arsenal, scoring just two goals in 14 appearances, while also providing three assists.

Gyokeres has started just one Premier League game to boot, having fallen behind Kai Havertz in the strikers' pecking order, but he remains indispensable for the Sweden national team.

Gyokeres and strike partner Alexander Isak led the line for Graham Potter's men against Bosnia, whom Sweden drew first blood against through Daniel Svensson with just five minutes gone.

Gyokeres doubled his nation's lead from the penalty spot shortly afterwards, before rifling home from 12 yards yet again on the stroke of half time, and Sweden survived a fightback attempt from their visitors to make it four wins from five.

By making the net bulge at the Strawberry Arena, Gyokeres scored for the eighth Nations League game running, becoming the first player in the history of the competition to achieve that feat.

Viktor Gyökeres has now scored in eight consecutive Nations League games for Sweden ?? 8 games played, 12 goals ? https://t.co/jOt5Hc5U6o

The 28-year-old already held the record for the most consecutive Nations League games scored in, as no other player has struck in more than six straight matches.

However, Gyokeres has now extended his unparalleled achievement; his closest challenger is England captain Harry Kane, who has scored in six consecutive Nations League matches and could make it seven on the spin when the Three Lions face Spain on Sunday.

Gyokeres's record run began in October 2024, when he netted once in a 3-0 win over Serbia, and the ex-Sporting Lisbon man also bagged against Slovakia and Azerbaijan in that year's tournament, scoring four against the latter.

Gyokeres now boasts six goals from five Nations League games in 2026-27, scoring in previous matches against Romania, Bosnia, Poland and Romania again before his Saturday double.

Not only did Gyokeres's brace on Saturday extend his successive scoring streak; the Arsenal forward has now overtaken Cristiano Ronaldo in the all-time Nations League scoring charts.

Ronaldo managed 15 Nations League goals for Portugal, but Gyokeres has now found the net 16 times in the competition, the second-most in the competition's history.

The Sweden star now only trails Erling Haaland in the list, as the Manchester City marksman has scored 23 Nations League goals for Norway after his strike in Saturday's victory over Wales.

Sweden have now moved onto 13 points from five games in League B Group 4, thus guaranteeing promotion to League A ahead of their last game against Poland on Tuesday.

#1867. Arsenal: Why Kepa Arrizabalaga was allowed to make second international debut amid surprise twist

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga has been in action during the international break, though not for the Spain national team.

The 32-year-old, who joined the Gunners from London rivals Chelsea in July 2025 for £5million, has 13 senior caps for La Roja, but has not made an appearance since a 2-0 loss to Scotland in March 2023.

Overlooked once again by Luis de la Fuente for Spain’s Nations League double-header against the Czech Republic and England in favour of Unai Simon, Joan Garcia and Arsenal team-mate David Raya, it was set to be a quiet international window for Kepa.

In a surprise turn of events, Kepa was called up to the Basque Country squad for their friendly against Venezuela and made his debut on Saturday, playing 45 minutes of the 1-0 win at San Mames.

While Athletic Club star Mikel Jauregizar scored the only goal of the game, some Arsenal fans may have been left wondering why their back-up goalkeeper was able to play for another national team.

Of course, it is well known that FIFA rules state that players cannot switch national teams after they've played three competitive fixtures.

However, despite Kepa winning 13 senior caps for Spain, he was cleared to play for the Basque Country because they are currently not recognised by FIFA.

As such, the win over Venezuela was not an official match, in the eyes of football's governing body.

Nevertheless, Kepa was able to get valuable minutes in his legs, having made just one appearance for Arsenal so far this season - the 4-2 win over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup third round.

Future Kepa appearances for the Basque Country could be in doubt as they have started the process to secure official international status for the national team.

Part of a statement reads: “The Basque Football Federation (EFF-FVF) has revived the process to obtain international official status for the Basque National Team, both men's and women's.

“With this aim, it has approached the Supreme Sports Council and has communicated information about the initiative to the Spanish Football Federation.”

#1866. Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after criticism from Liverpool legend

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness said on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice said: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he said. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’
