Speaking on Sky Sport’s ‘Calcio Unplugged’, Igli Tare revealed all to Gianluca Di Marzio and Stefano Borghi in an in-depth interview about his time with the Diavolo, as Radio Rossonera has relayed.

“Today is the first time I’ve spoken out after all these months. The wound of not having reached the Champions League is still enormous, and since I arrived at Milan – also questioning myself with the type of contract I signed – the objective couldn’t be only the Champions League; otherwise I wouldn’t have understood where I was.”

“It was great because he was the one who convinced me. He had such a huge desire to join Milan. I wanted to video chat before going to see him because I couldn’t believe it. But after five minutes, I knew in my head that he was the player Milan really lacked.

“Not just because of his qualities, but as a man and as a figure that that team didn’t have. He never said no. A photo with a child, an autograph, a meeting, talking to someone… He never said no. These are the things that humility is key to in life.

“I’m proud to have brought a great champion to Milan. In my opinion, if he wants, he can play another two seasons without any problem. He never missed a training session. Sometimes we were the ones to stop him because he was always there, ready. Loving football at that age is truly an honour.”

Is it a characteristic of the champion or is it a generational issue? Today’s champions seem to have a different mentality:

“Today we live in the age of social media. At 16, you’re already a footballer who can earn millions of euros. Living this way, you have the problem of not only managing a player, who is still a child, but you have to manage the business they bring with them: family, agents, girlfriends…

“These are obstacles that didn’t exist back then. We were a generation that played in the streets. Back then, our parents beat us to get us to come home. Today, however, it’s to get them out of the house because they spend all day in front of computers.

“This aspect has been lost a bit, but it’s our fault. Education and discipline are the key to success.”

Fullkrug. He performed poorly in Milan, but in the Bundesliga he’s scoring a lot and is the top scorer. How do you explain that?

“It’s simple. He came to us after a tough time in England, with a lot of scepticism. And then, right away, he broke his toe. No one ever said he’d been having injections on the bone for two months just to train, let alone to play.

“I knew he was a centre forward that the team was missing; given his characteristics and his interpretation of the game, his qualities were unquestionable. Just two years before coming to Milan, he’d played in the Champions League final, playing a key role in a competition with Borussia Dortmund.

“There are situations where, for a player, even a very important one, it matters how you feel. If you feel appreciated, valued, taken into consideration… When you play for a club like Milan, the weight of the shirt is completely different than when you play for other clubs.

“You feel it from the first day you join. I had no doubt that he could be what he’s demonstrating now.”

“We tried to sign him back in June. We made a first attempt. In the final days of the transfer window, another important name we tried to sign was Akanji. The Champions League was crucial for both of them. They turned him down, not because of the club’s importance, but because he wasn’t playing in the Champions League.

“Then the opportunity arose again at the end of August for Rabiot. Defeat against Cremonese? No, we had already decided to bring him. It was just a matter of contract details.”

“It was difficult for us because we decided to change the formation five days before the transfer window closed. Switching from a 4-3-3 to a three-man defense meant we were having a really hard time finding a quality player in the last five days.

“We were a bit unlucky, first with the Akanji story and then with Liverpool’s Joe Gomez… Guehi’s move from Crystal Palace to Liverpool fell through, and at the last minute they—we already had the deal ready, we were just waiting for this to happen—made a step back. And to avoid being left without a central defender at the last minute, we signed Odogu as a promising player.”

On not being able to reach the Champions League and not being able to continue his work at Milan…

“This is the first time today, after all these months, that I’ve spoken about this… The wound of not reaching the Champions League is still enormous. I think that from the first day I arrived at Milan, even in the way I signed—I questioned myself with the type of contract.

“I said, ‘If I have to come only for the Champions League objective, then I don’t understand where I’ve come from.’ Milan has a different story. I had to go through a trial. The disappointment is that those who run the club didn’t understand how much time people needed, which is now being done, rightly so.

“That is to say, it takes several transfer sessions to get a competitive team ready to win. At the beginning, I felt the responsibility to put the pieces together immediately, because after the defeat in the Coppa Italia final the year before, there were some important signs.

“I didn’t know where to start. But I think we did an important job last summer, we sold for a lot and also signed 10 new players. Then you need time to integrate, learn new philosophies and create a cohesive group, hungry to win.

“Until March-April, we were a group with difficulties, but we were at the top of the table. Then in the last 10 matchdays, we had a mental breakdown, also due to other external dynamics, which I don’t want to discuss here, which had a significant impact.

“Internal or external dynamics? External to the team. But we also have some blame: myself first and foremost, along with Max [Allegri].

“We had to be a little more attentive to certain dynamics. We needed to be more present with the team to ultimately lead them to the final result. Isolation is the wrong word; I don’t believe in these things. I believe in teamwork; I believe in cohesion: from the club to the team.

“When this happens, you transmit it to the team. When these situations become possible, you could also see it in the team’s results, because the players are very attentive. Sometimes we think they have other interests, but they pay attention to everything that comes out. They follow everything very carefully and transmit it.

“Instilling serenity… How can you convey serenity? When, in difficult moments, you show that you believe in the project more than before. Sometimes I missed this feeling, a lack of something that could give us the final push.”

But despite this, did you think you could continue? Does this farewell after only a year feel like a stab in the back?

“Look, I would have asked for a round table where we could all sit down together and analyze everything. Then they could have just said ‘no, thanks’… But I respect the decision they made. I accept it with great regret, but I’ve never questioned it because there’s someone above me who has to decide, including for the fate of the club.

“And when they decide to take a different path, you have to accept it. I know things could have gone differently, even much better. I’ll always be a Milan fan, even after an experience like that.”

Was AC Milan a team that needed the constant presence of a manager or coach to avoid letting itself go as it later did?

“The feeling I had at the beginning was that this leadership was a bit lacking. The arrival of Modric—and another of our goals was also Granit Xhaka, Leverkusen’s captain—was precisely to bring real players into the group, with important characteristics and capable of leading others.

“Granit didn’t arrive; Luka arrived, who has a different way of being a leader: he does it in silence and with his attitude on the pitch. I had the opportunity to meet Mike Maignan: an extraordinary guy, a soul who cares deeply about the AC Milan shirt.

“Gabbia is another extraordinary guy; he lives for this club. Rabiot too… His experience spoke for itself. The great disappointment is that I expected something more in terms of responsibility and leadership from Pulisic: he’s a top-class player with unquestionable qualities. But in terms of performance, things happened that I had never experienced in my career…

“Like Gimenez: an extraordinary guy with numbers that spoke for themselves; for a year he failed to score a goal. Then it happened that Pulisic didn’t score for six months. He scored a goal. Then Leao didn’t score for four months.

“Situations that are hard to come by in football have happened… It can happen that you don’t score for a month, two months, but that long a period of time also affected the team’s final performance.

“Losing a match against Cagliari the way we did, 2-1, I think was the worst match of my life. The feeling and the disappointment I felt towards the fans in the stadium that night is something I will never forget for the rest of my life.”

If Cardinale had been the Cardinale he is today, the one who is also physically present, would you still be AC ​​Milan’s DS?

“I can’t answer that question; he has to answer it. I can say that I remember when the Jashari negotiations were going on… I had just landed in Rome and I was very pleased when he called me because he wanted to understand what was happening in that negotiation.

“I explained all the dynamics to him and I really liked that he said, ‘Anything you need, if you have to spend a little more, let me know because I’m here.’ Then during that process I never had the chance to talk to him, even intentionally.

“There were other people above me who I never wanted to bypass. I never had a direct relationship with him, and the possibility of a discussion would have helped everyone. Not me, but everyone. By putting all the problems and dynamics on the table, we could have resolved things much sooner. But I think it’s a new experience for Cardinale.

“He’s had experience in other sports in America. Now he’s done something important, taking responsibility and putting his face on the line. I would have preferred to have had that presence even when I was there because it would have been very useful. But for the Milan, better late than never.

“Now, for better or worse, he will make his own decisions and responsibilities. I think that for him, too, the best interests of Milan come first.”

Was Leao a problem or a resource in your mind?

“I knew him from the outside. When I had the chance to meet him in person, I thought he was an extraordinary guy. I truly loved him as a person, like everyone else. But he was the player from whom we all expected something more. I think football was no longer a priority for him. That’s the key to understanding him.”

“I think a bit about his life outside of football. Music, fashion, things… But I never doubted the sense of belonging he had towards Milan. You could sense that he loved playing for Milan and was suffering from not performing.

“He had many physical problems… First a calf, then a bit of pubalgia… He always played with his hands under control. I always tried to have individual conversations with him more than with any other Milan player.

“Every time I spoke to him, I left with a positive feeling. I sensed that he wanted to. But sometimes wanting isn’t enough.”

Was there a chance that Leao would leave during your summer too?

“A concrete offer never came for him. Regarding the other transfers, it’s not just Tare’s job. When I arrived – even at Lazio – I was a bit alone, but I tried to involve all the members of the club to give him the importance he needed to build a sense of belonging and responsibility. I think I did a very good job, together with Furlani, Ibra, and Moncada.

“We achieved significant sales figures, in a year when we weren’t even in the Champions League. Thanks to the work we did last summer, investments were made this year, with the money we had at the time. I really believe in teamwork.

“I said it even before the Coppa Italia match against Bari; I asked to speak to convey the importance of the work of the people within the club because it was right that way. Then afterwards, it’s human…

“They were coming off a bad year, when two cumbersome figures like Tare and Allegri arrive, and everyone was talking about Tare and Allegri, some disappointment was understandable. I understood the feeling they had, but I could… There was little to do about it.

“For me, it was a new path, a new opportunity. It was essential to work as a team and present ourselves as a real company.”

#1863. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Sir Alex Ferguson ahead of Man Utd mission

Mauricio Pochettino would welcome the chance to speak with Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares for the task of resurrecting Manchester United.

Michael Carrick’s successor’s penultimate match in charge of United States ended in an emphatic 6-0 thrashing of Haiti as he moved a step closer to beginning his United tenure.

The former Tottenham boss will start life at the Red Devils on Wednesday after two Nations League matches with Haiti, but USA all but assured their place in the semi-finals of the competition with a comprehensive first-leg showing.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

Pochettino paid tribute to his staff and players in an emotional press conference on Friday and duly watched USA romp to a 6-0 victory.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We played for him,’ Trusty said in a post-match interview with TNT Sports after opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

‘Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. It’s a great opportunity that he’s moving on to. But we played for him. It’s his team. It’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match.’

The second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals will take place Tuesday in Cincinnati.

‘Pochettino is an amazing manager and he added a lot to us with the national team,’ Folarin Balogun told TNT Sports. ‘It’s always sad to see a top coach leave but it’s a part of the sport.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The 54-year-old will have little time to reflect on his accomplishments in his soon-to-be former role as he will immediately begin plotting for his first game in charge of United at Anfield next Sunday.

Pochettino inherits a side that is currently in the bottom three in the Premier League table, short on confidence and a dressing room split following the recent actions of senior players, including the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez.

Given the current state of play and his pre-existing relationship with Ferguson, it is perhaps no surprise that Pochettino is seeking the advice of the club’s greatest ever manager as he prepares to embark on arguably the toughest assignment of his managerial career to date.

‘Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,’ Pochettino told Telegraph Sport when asked if he had been in contact with Ferguson.

‘I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

‘For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense.

‘But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.’

Brazilian legend Ronaldinho will, this afternoon, make his first competitive appearance in more than a decade.

The former Barcelona and AC Milan has not played competitively since featuring for Fluminense in September 2015, though that will change on Sunday as he is confirmed to start for Italian third division side Ravenna against local rivals Forli.

"He will play from the start, there's no doubt," Ravenna boss Andrea Mandorlini told reporters. "Then together we will decide how long he plays.

"He is one of the greatest players of the modern era. And we have to get a result. We always play with three forwards. He will be one of the three."

This will be Ronaldinho’s long-awaited debut for the Serie C side after joining the club in August, with footage emerging on social media over the weekend to prove the 46-year-old has not lost a step.

Ravenna are currently sitting in second place - six points behind leaders Spezia - in the Serie C, Group B table and have won four of their last five matches, including the last three in a row.

Speaking in August after announcing his comeback, Ronaldinho revealed his target was to score his 300th career goal having initially retired on 299.

Bruno Fernandes will delay any decision on a new Manchester United contract until he has made up his mind on new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The Sun report that Manchester United remain confident Fernandes will sign a new contract, but that his decision is based on how things play out under new boss Pochettino.

#1859. Vinicius Junior matches previous 46-game Brazil goal tally in 12 matches

By Naim Beneddra | 15 Nov 2026 07:55

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior has matched his goalscoring tally from his previous 46 Brazil appearances in just 12 international matches, completing a remarkable reversal in fortunes while enduring one of his most difficult periods at club level.

The 26-year-old scored twice during Brazil's 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan in Singapore on Saturday, producing two outstanding finishes to temporarily rescue Carlo Ancelotti's side from a two-goal deficit.

Despite the result, Vinicius extended an impressive international scoring run that stands in stark contrast to his struggles under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid this season. The winger has now registered eight goals and three assists across his last 12 appearances for the Selecao.

Remarkably, he had scored just eight times in his previous 46 international matches, a record that frequently attracted criticism given his outstanding performances for Madrid.

The latest brace takes his overall international tally to 16 goals in 58 appearances, with Brazil increasingly becoming the environment in which he produces his best football.

For much of his international career, Vinicius struggled to reproduce the performances that established him among the world's leading attacking players.

His difficulties were particularly evident at the 2024 Copa America, when he failed to consistently influence Brazil's campaign despite arriving after another outstanding season with Real Madrid.

The situation has changed considerably in recent months.

Vinicius responded to criticism following Brazil's disappointing performance against France in March and has since developed into one of the team's most reliable attacking outlets.

He scored in all three group-stage matches at the 2026 World Cup, helping Brazil finish ahead of Morocco before their elimination against Norway in the last 16.

Although he failed to find the net in that defeat, his performances during the tournament provided further evidence of his growing importance to Ancelotti.

Saturday's friendly against Japan offered another demonstration.

With Brazil trailing 2-0 following early goals from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura, Vinicius pulled one back in the 33rd minute, collecting a pass from Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes before firing an unstoppable effort into the top corner.

The Real Madrid attacker was less convincing in other phases of the encounter, losing possession on several occasions and struggling to make an impact against Japan's organised defence.

However, he produced another moment of individual brilliance in the 75th minute.

Receiving possession following a short corner, Vinicius cut inside Yukinari Sugawara and unleashed a powerful strike that struck both posts before crossing the line.

His equaliser appeared to have earned Brazil a draw, only for Coventry City's Tatsuhiro Sakamoto to score the winner in stoppage time.

The defeat left Ancelotti with questions to answer about Brazil's defensive organisation, but Vinicius's finishing provided another encouraging sign ahead of the team's final international fixture of 2026.

The transformation in Vinicius's international performances is particularly striking given his current situation at the Santiago Bernabeu.

The Brazilian has managed just one goal and three assists in 12 appearances for Real Madrid this season, struggling to establish any consistency under Mourinho.

His problems intensified after he received a four-match domestic suspension following his red card against Villarreal in October.

Madrid subsequently won all four La Liga matches during his absence, while summer signing Yan Diomande took advantage of the opportunity to establish himself as an alternative on the left flank.

The emergence of the Ivory Coast international has raised questions about Vinicius's previously unquestioned place in the starting lineup.

However, Mourinho has publicly backed the Brazilian to rediscover his best form, insisting that the club will continue supporting him through a difficult period.

The Portuguese manager has also acknowledged that performances, rather than reputation, must determine selection decisions.

Madrid's attacking hierarchy has become increasingly competitive, with Kylian Mbappe maintaining an exceptional goalscoring rate and Diomande providing greater defensive involvement on the left.

That contrast was highlighted when Marc Cucurella defended Vinicius against comparisons with Diomande earlier this month.

Vinicius's latest performances for Brazil offer an encouraging reminder of the qualities that made him a decisive figure in two Champions League triumphs.

His eight international goals across 12 matches represent an average of one every 1.5 appearances, compared with one every 5.75 games during his previous 46 outings.

He will have an opportunity to extend that sequence when Brazil face Singapore on Tuesday, November 17.

Four days later, Madrid return to La Liga action against Celta Vigo, when Mourinho will have to decide whether Vinicius's renewed international confidence merits an immediate return to the starting lineup.

Matteo Gabbia has admitted that he could return to the field in January for AC Milan, but he doesn’t want to rush back.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This season, though, it seems Gerry Cardinale is going to go down a different route and spend to help Ruben Amorim with his defensive options. Indeed, there have been plenty of rumours about recruitments at the back.

However, Gabbia could again be a key returnee in January, with him hoping to return from injury early in the new year.

Speaking to Sky Sport (via MilanNews) – at an event organised by the Milan Foundation at Milan’s “Arturo Toscanini” secondary school, where they met with several children with disabilities – Gabbia discussed the importance of the event, as well as his recovery.

“It’s wonderful, very enjoyable to spend hours with them. It’s also beautiful to see how they manage to create a group, something that really shows the importance of teamwork, the importance of friendship, even among themselves.

“We’re happy; we thank Fondazione Milan for the project, which is always beautiful and important: we’re happy to be a part of it and we’re enjoying the afternoon.”

Are you able to rejoin the group in January?

“Yes, that could be the time: we’re trying to work hard and do everything as best we can. I obviously have to thank the physiotherapists and the doctor because we’re really doing everything we can every day to try to heal the injury and get back on the pitch feeling good.

“It’s definitely been an unlucky season for me so far: I don’t want it to happen again or for any recurrences, so it’s also important to take the right time, get back in shape, and support the team right now.”

“Although it’s bad for the team that there are so many injured players, we’re together right now, supporting each other and trying to encourage each other through therapy, gym work, and the entire recovery process. Therefore, we’re trying to work as a team this week too, to overcome all the players’ injuries.

“From a personal standpoint, I’m trying to take this time calmly, in the sense that these things are part of sport, part of life, and not all moments are the same.

“This is certainly a difficult time, but it still allows me to stay close to the team, to try to lend my support, even in the good and bad times. That’s what I’m doing, in addition to obviously doing what I can to try to return as soon as possible and make my contribution on the pitch.”

How do you explain the team’s ups and downs?

“I think it’s something we need to get our heads around; we need to understand the importance of every game.

“The other day I heard our coach give an interview in which he said something important: we need to understand that every game, when you don’t win, is taken as a defeat, a heavy defeat. We need to truly understand the importance of every game and approach training to prepare 100%, as best as possible, for every match.

“Therefore, I think this is room for improvement, but I see a group that is really eager to improve, to work, and as a result, I’m sure we’ll be able to fix this flaw as well.

“Although we’ve had a good start to the year in the league and less so in the Europa League, we have plenty of time to improve and have a strong year.”

#1842. Kevin De Bruyne responds to PSV Eindhoven transfer amid Napoli exit rumours

By Naim Beneddra | 15 Nov 2026 08:10

Former Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne has refused to rule out a surprise January move to PSV Eindhoven, with the Dutch champions reportedly making contact over a potential deal to end his difficult spell at Napoli.

The 35-year-old Belgium international has emerged as an ambitious transfer target for PSV, who are exploring the possibility of bringing him back to the Netherlands after just 18 months in Italian football.

According to Dutch publication Voetbal International, PSV have already approached De Bruyne's representatives, with preliminary discussions taking place over a potential winter transfer.

The former Premier League star addressed the speculation following Belgium's 2-1 Nations League victory over Turkey on Thursday, a match in which he scored.

While De Bruyne insisted that he remains happy with his current physical condition and performances, he stopped short of dismissing the possibility of leaving Napoli.

His response comes amid reports of growing uncertainty surrounding his future under Massimiliano Allegri, with PSV hoping to take advantage of his contractual situation.

Speaking to Belgian broadcaster VTM Nieuws after the Turkey match, De Bruyne was asked directly about reports linking him with a move to Eindhoven.

"I can't say too much about it. At the moment I'm happy," the midfielder explained.

"I feel good, I'm playing every match at a good level. And what comes, comes. It's not the time to talk about it now.

"I know how it works. There are always lots of rumours. I stay calm about it – you know me. I'm happy with my level and how I feel physically. That's all that matters."

Asked whether PSV's interest was mutual, De Bruyne offered a brief response: "We'll see."

His comments followed reports in the Netherlands that PSV had begun assessing the financial conditions required to secure his signature.

Voetbal International confirmed that the Eredivisie club had made enquiries and established contact with the player, although the publication stressed that their interest remained at an early stage.

Italian newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport has subsequently reported that PSV also approached Napoli to clarify the club's intentions regarding De Bruyne's contract.

The Belgian's current agreement expires in June 2027, but Napoli hold an option to extend it by another season.

That clause could prove important to negotiations, with the Italian side yet to confirm whether they would consider allowing their experienced playmaker to leave midway through the campaign.

Belgium manager Mark van Bommel, who previously played for and managed PSV, believes the Dutch club could offer De Bruyne a suitable environment.

"He has to make the decision himself, but he doesn't live far away and Dutch football suits him," Van Bommel told VTM Nieuws.

"The attacking way of playing, always wanting to play football, that fits him."

Current PSV manager Peter Bosz has also spoken highly of De Bruyne in the past, describing him as one of the greatest players in football history.

De Bruyne joined Napoli on a free transfer in the summer of 2025 following a decade at Manchester City, where he established himself as one of the Premier League's greatest midfielders.

However, his first season in Italy was disrupted by a hamstring injury that sidelined him for more than four months.

Napoli also failed to retain their Serie A title, while De Bruyne subsequently criticised former manager Antonio Conte's defensive approach.

The Belgian explained that he had struggled to operate in his preferred position and questioned the team's attacking ambition under the Italian.

Conte's replacement, Allegri, has not brought the improvement in results Napoli had hoped for.

The club sit 10th in Serie A after 11 matches and have lost three of their opening four Champions League fixtures, increasing scrutiny of their performances.

De Bruyne has also experienced reported disagreements with Allegri over his tactical role, although he remains an important member of the side.

Indeed, he has featured in all 15 of Napoli's competitive matches this season, contributing four goals and two assists.

His availability and productivity suggest that a January departure would not simply be the consequence of losing his place in the starting lineup.

There is also a personal dimension to the speculation.

De Bruyne's wife, Michele Lacroix, spoke in September about the family's difficulties adapting to life in Naples and their desire to return to Belgium.

"We want to live here, in Limburg. The sooner, the better," she told Belgian magazine NINA.

"Kevin leads a very limited life in Naples. It's not much fun for him. Besides, we can't do anything together as a family in the city."

Eindhoven's proximity to the Belgian border could make PSV an appealing destination, although De Bruyne has not publicly linked his family's circumstances to a possible transfer.

The midfielder has also been linked with a return to the Premier League through Everton, who were reportedly assessing their chances of securing his services earlier this month.

For PSV, the main obstacles remain Napoli's willingness to negotiate and the financial demands involved in signing a player of De Bruyne's stature.

With no agreement in place, his latest comments leave the possibility of a January move open without indicating that a departure has been decided.

#1840. How Thomas Tuchel instilled winning England instinct to secure historic victory over Spain

When Thomas Tuchel and his England coaching staff come to reflect on England’s sensational victory in Spain, they will come to the conclusion it could scarcely have gone better.

Such a statement may feel bizarre given the visitors were at one stage 3-0 up with cruise control applied, before another Jarell Quansah error led to an Elliot Anderson red card, a penalty converted, and then a second goal back for a Spain team totally rejuvenated.

The reality, though, is that if England’s canter to a one-sided victory had continued as it was doing, Tuchel and his team would have far less to pore over as they unpick the headers and volleys at the end of this calendar year and the learning they can take from what still finished - by getting over the line 3-2 and topping the group - a hugely successful international break.

Tuchel had repeatedly described this affair as “a final” in the days leading up, but just as important as finishing top of the group and the potentially easier quarter-final opponent it could secure them in March was delivering a performance to provide encouragement that the Three Lions can indeed go toe-to-toe with the very best and avoid unforced errors in the process.

OK, there was one such mistake: Quansah, at fault for Croatia’s goal at Wembley on Thursday, dawdling on the ball and conceding possession cheaply. England’s magnificent earlier work threatened to unravel at that point as the dominoes of the resultant red card, goal and second strike fell.

But then came the memories of the cavalry this summer, their resolute World Cup closing-it-out jobs against Mexico and then Norway and then the ugly attempt to do it all over again at the semi-final against Argentina. Instinct kicked in.

James Trafford getting the nod ahead of Jordan Pickford in the Spanish capital was a bold call, as was Ben White starting at right-back and Lewis Hall on the left, but all three were superb, as the head coach’s big decisions were wholly vindicated. The world champions’ unbeaten run was ended by England, the Spanish tasting defeat in Madrid for the first time in 39 years, since a certain Gary Lineker netted all four in a 4-2 England win.

Lamine Yamal posed England all sorts of questions from the right wing - a fabulous player - but did he cause them a wealth of problems? Aside from a simple assist for Spain’s second, no, not really. Hall was sturdy at left-back, just as England were all over the pitch.

Their first-half display, after which point they led 1-0 through a Harry Kane penalty, was described by Roy Keane in ITV’s coverage as “perfect”. They had certainly all been on the same wavelength, their passing sequences all crisp. And in the second half, after those two quickfire goals shipped, the defensive equivalent of that joined-up thinking was visible from a team that looked like one.

The players involved in this Nations League group game represent many of the Champions League powerhouses and yet there was no hint of this being an unwanted match that disrupts the club football juggernaut and where there is a needless risk of injury. Not a bit of that. When Jude Bellingham’s number came up and he was substituted in the 83rd minute, presumably to keep Real Madrid happy, he looked angered not to be carrying on in a game that had just about everything. What’s more: it had the result that England craved. And expected.

“We knew we were going to beat them tonight,” said Declan Rice. Not only a thrilling night for England, it will also have taught them plenty about themselves. That is just as important.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Tuchel continued on Trafford: ‘Very good. That’s his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.

‘The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.’

The German has also liked what he has seen from Trafford on the ball, saying: ‘There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

‘Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half.

‘With everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.’

At 24 years old, Trafford is eight years younger than Pickford and looks to be his successor, even if he has not entirely displaced him just yet.

The win in Spain meant England topped their Nations League group and will play a runner-up from another group in the quarter-finals of the competition.

Groups A2 and A4 come to an end on Monday and Tuesday respectively, which is when we will learn England’s possible opponents for Friday’s draw.

Belgium have already secured second place in group A1, so they are a possible opponent for the Three Lions in the quarter-finals that are played in March next year.

#1837. Man Utd told Chelsea star would be ‘good signing’ for Mauricio Pochettino

Mikael Silvestre has encouraged Manchester United to explore a move for Estevao – but doubts the forward could be coaxed to the Theatre of Dreams as he appears intent on ‘fighting for his place’ at Chelsea.

United spent in the region of £160million on new signings in the summer, with club chiefs showing they were prepared to back Michael Carrick following an impressive third-place finish.

But any optimism that had grown amongst the fanbase in the back-end of last season rapidly faded as a 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea last month extended the Red Devils’ miserable winless run to nine matches in all competitions.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Naturally, attentions have quickly turned towards the January transfer window, when United will be expected to splash the cash in the hope of boosting their prospects for the second half of the campaign.

United chiefs are set to resurrect their pursuit of a left-back as a priority to provide support for Luke Shaw after missing out on Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

According to Silvestre, Chelsea winger Estevao could represent a ‘good signing’ for United, with the Brazilian having made just one start in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That start happened to come against United, though, and the 19-year-old was widely praised for his performance as goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer proved decisive at Stamford Bridge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Well, Estevao played against United for Chelsea, and I think he’s shown why he should feature more,’ Silvestre told Betarades.gr.

‘It looks like he’s going to fight for his place in the team, so I don’t anticipate United making a move for him.

‘But he’s a good player for sure. He’s playing for the national team of Brazil, and I like his style. If he were available, he would be a good signing for United.’

Asked why Newcastle and England star Hall may ‘make sense’ for United at left-back, Silvestre replied: ‘Lewis Hall had an impressive season with Newcastle, and he’s been on the club’s radar for sure.

‘The club made an attempt to sign him and other fullbacks, but couldn’t get it done.

‘They now have to rely on Luke Shaw, Diego Dalot, on Noussair Mazraoui, and on Patrick Dorgu, who has also been injured for quite some time. So that’s not been helpful either.’

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

The international break is never really a period of major news, yet Milan broke that spell today. Indeed, RedBird Capital Partners published a statement about a new company formed to oversee all of the Rossoneri’s business.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A centralised company that would allow everything Diavolo to be kept in one place is a major step forward for the club and city. San Donato was mentioned as an important focus for the new company, but the headline will remain the footballing operation.

To help with the project, Gerry Cardinale – who spoke about the decision – has appointed Brett Yormark to be the CEO of the company and reports suggest that he will join in January.

“It is an honour and a privilege to take on this role in a city with Milan’s history and passion for sports. I understand the responsibility that comes with leading an organisation tied to institutions that mean so much to their fans and the communities they serve.

#1835. Jurgen Klopp gushing in praise for Arsenal star: ‘He is a complete package’

Jurgen Klopp has talked up Arsenal’s Kai Havertz as ‘a complete package as a top player’ as he hopes the forward can have a big impact for Germany.

The 27-year-old has won 64 caps for his country, scoring 25 goals, and was in action as Germany beat Serbia 3-1 on Friday.

The former Chelsea man will be in the team on Monday night for the crucial Nations League clash with Netherlands, as Klopp looks to take his side into the quarter-finals.

The Germany boss has looked to build confidence in Havertz by talking up the forward’s qualities, which he feels can match up to almost anyone in the game.

#1834. Thomas Tuchel reveals key reason why England beat Spain in ‘best performance’ of his tenure

Thomas Tuchel has explained why England’s 3-2 win over Spain was the best performance of his tenure.

The German has been in charge of the Three Lions since January 2025 and guided them to third place at the World Cup in the summer, their highest finish in the competition since their only title in 1966.

That included memorable wins against Croatia, DR Congo and Mexico. Last month, in the Nations League, England inflicted upon Croatia the heaviest defeat in their history as they thrashed Slaven Bilic’s side 7-0 in Rijeka.

But Tuchel admitted he views Sunday’s 10-man victory over the world champions in Madrid as the finest performance during his time at the helm.

Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored for the Three Lions as they ended the world champions’ 43-game unbeaten streak despite conceding twice in the second half. It secured England top spot in their Nations League group ahead of Spain.

“Brilliant performance,” Tuchel told ITV after the game. “A well deserved win. Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

“It was a complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit-wise, energy-wise and also football quality was highest level.

“We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.”

Speaking about how England dug in defensively once Spain had scored their second goal, Tuchel said: “Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]. That’s the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners.”

Asked what England showed, he replied: “What we are made of and what we can do. We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years [at the World Cup] and we weren’t happy with it. It’s impressive what we did in the last two camps.”

#1831. Man City beat Real Madrid again as £130k-a-week star 'close' to signing new contract

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 08:18

Manchester City are reportedly on the verge of agreeing a new deal with midfielder-turned-defender Matheus Nunes.

The former Wolverhampton Wanderers man is still on the same terms he agreed upon his arrival in 2023, and he is currently due to become a free agent in 2028.

However, Nunes has become a key figure for the Sky Blues at right-back, managing a combined 13 assists across the last two Premier League campaigns after switching from a central midfield role.

Nunes started 32 Premier League matches in Pep Guardiola's farewell season last term, although he is yet to score or assist in 10 games across all competitions in the current season.

Nevertheless, the Portugal international's contributions have not gone unnoticed, and according to the Manchester Evening News, a renewal is close to being sealed.

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho is supposedly interested in signing Nunes, but City have no intention of letting the 28-year-old go and are in talks over a new three-year agreement.

Nunes is believed to be earning around £130,000 a week at the Etihad Stadium, but his new deal would include a £20k-a-week pay rise, taking him up to £150,000 a week.

The defender would subsequently be on the same salary as midfielders Mateo Kovacic and Ayyoub Bouaddi, and City are supposedly confident of retaining his services despite lingering uncertainty over their charges appeal.

Having been found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules, Man City - who have always vehemently denied the charges - could lose their Premier League status if their appeal against the charges outcome fails.

Nevertheless, the Sky Blues have supposedly stressed that their players remain content at the Etihad, and it should only be a matter of time before Nunes's new deal is announced.

The 28-year-old signed for Man City from Wolves for £51.7m in the summer of 2023, since when he has scored five goals and set up 25 more in 131 games for the club in all tournaments.

Nunes has won the Premier League, Club World Cup, FA Cup, EFL Cup and Community Shield at the Etihad Stadium and was also called up to Portugal's World Cup 2026 squad, but he played just one minute in North America.

Nunes is one of four City players who could depart for nothing in either 2027 or 2028; Kovacic and Marcus Bettinelli are due to become free agents next year, while backup goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is out of contract at the end of next season.

Amid concerns over Gianluigi Donnarumma's form, Rulli may be in line for an extension if he earns a shot in between the sticks and manages to prove himself, although the Argentinian is already 34 years old.

Meanwhile, Ruben Dias and Vitor Reis both see their deals expire in 2029, but the former will likely be in line for at least a new short-term deal in the not-so-distant future.

#1830. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1829. Chelsea injury update: Joao Pedro, Emi Martinez, Josh Acheampong latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea could welcome back two key players from injury as Premier League action resumes this weekend at home to Leeds.

The Blues went into the final international break of the year on the back of a crushing defeat to Sunderland as Xabi Alonso’s side had no response to Enzo Le Fee’s penalty - which was awarded a few minutes after Cole Palmer had controversially seen a claim for a spot-kick of his own turned down following a VAR review.

As such, Chelsea have dropped down to fifth in the table, though there is likely to be some positive news regarding Emi Martinez and Joao Pedro - who both missed the loss to Sunderland - in the next few days.

With that in mind, here is the latest Chelsea injury news and return dates…

Josh Acheampong was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea matchday squad at the Stadium of Light, particularly as the youngster had started all five matches prior.

It quickly became clear, via Alonso, that the defender was dealing with a minor issue. The good news is Acheampong is not expected to be sidelined for an extended period, though he was forced to withdraw from England U21 duty.

“He is recovering from a minor thing. He missed the fitness to be ready for today but we are expecting that he will be back after the international break,” Alonso said of Acheampong before the defeat to Sunderland. “It’s a pity because he was in a good moment.”

After the game, the Chelsea manager added:“There are situations. Yesterday Josh felt something and he was not fit to play. So we are shorter in options and we need to go through this time.

“Even when we win, or when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting to have them back because they are important.

“Now we need to use the time to recover them, but with the players we have, we have to get ready for the next one.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

Martinez has now missed Chelsea's last four games across all competitions after undergoing surgery for a broken jaw sustained upon a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite in the win over Everton last month.

The Argentina international was expected to be sidelined for around six weeks, but has made a swift recovery. He returned to training ahead of the Sunderland game and was in contention for a start, but it was ultimately decided that he would not be risked.

"He has made a great effort to be available but probably it was too rash, too risky [to be selected],” Alonso said.

“So he will use one more week, 10 days, to keep on training and get used to the mask. I’m sure after the break he will be available.”

Martinez was an unused substitute in Argentina’s 2-1 friendly defeat to Uruguay and may make his return to action against Costa Rica on Tuesday.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

Joao Pedro was forced to sit out Chelsea’s rare home loss to Tottenham due to picking up a thigh injury in training on the eve of the game.

No definitive timeframe has yet been set for the return of the Brazilian but Alonso has promised to have more news on the Brazilian - not selected for international duty - ahead of the Leeds game.

"No, not really updates,” Alonso said before the trip to Sunderland. “For sure, we are not expecting them for [Sunday].

“Let’s see after the international break the recovery that they [have] made. Ahead of the Leeds game, I will have more [news] but not today.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

Chelsea’s influential captain Reece James suffered a knee injury in training at Cobham on his return from another hamstring issue.

After consulting with a specialist, he underwent successful surgery last month that was described as “minor” and Alonso has been reluctant to put a date on his potential return.

However, Standard Sport understands that it is likely to be around three months before James is back in action.

Maxence Lacroix limped off late in the first half of the Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out defeat to Liverpool with a suspected hamstring injury.

Alonso said that Chelsea would need to assess the problem before estimating a recovery time, later admitting that he would be out until after the November international break.

“Max picked up an injury and we expect that he will not be ready before the international break. So he will be a few weeks out,” Alonso said before the win over Manchester United.

Reports have since suggested that Chelsea fear Lacroix, like James, may not play again until the New Year.

However, Alonso has said he will know more about the severity of Frenchman’s injury after the international break.

Jorrel Hato was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea squad that travelled to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup fourth round and has subsequently missed games against Man United and Sunderland.

Following the 2-0 win over the Red Devils, Alonso revealed that the Dutchman was battling a back injury and the recent update suggests Hato could return after the international break.

"No, no, no — he is not fit,” Alonso said of the Dutchman in the pre-Sunderland press conference. “It will take him some more weeks to be fit.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

Jamie Gittens has yet to make a single Premier League appearance for Chelsea so far this season, with his only two outings to date coming against Luton and Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

The winger has been so unlucky with injuries since arriving in west London from Borussia Dortmund last summer, a trend which continued as he suffered an ankle problem while on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month and needed crutches.

Alonso’s last update confirmed that Gittens was still facing “weeks” on the sidelines, putting him on track to return at some point in November or perhaps even early December.

Potential return date: November or December

#1828. Belgian journalist admits Sylla may be ‘more inclined’ to move to England: “His dream destination”

AC Milan have been heavily interested in Massire Sylla recently, but it seems they may struggle to sign him, let alone in January.

It’s no secret that Milan want to sign a central defender and whilst Goncalo Inacio is the leading name, he’s not the only one in the mix. Instead, there are several public names of interest and Sylla is one of them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

First linked by Matteo Moretto, his name has become more popular in reports linking the Rossoneri to defenders and he seems like a concrete target for the January mercato. Yet, it seems like it will be difficult to bring him to San Siro.

Speaking to MilanNews, Het Nieuwsblad journalist Tjorven Messiaen looked at Massire Sylla and what his future had in store.

In Italy, there’s been talk of AC Milan’s interest in Sylla. What’s being said about him in Belgium?

“I saw that AC Milan have linked him with him. In Belgium, we discovered him through social media, and the USG hasn’t confirmed anything yet. It’s possible, however, that AC Milan has drawn attention to the boy, because he’s playing great football.

“His move to AC Milan is unlikely to materialise in January, however, as both Sylla and the club would be more inclined to listen to offers from the Premier League. He’s the kind of player who would be a perfect fit for the English league.”

What are his main strengths and best qualities?

“He’s young, he’s good in duels, he’s quick. He’s also very good at ball control. He’s a complete defender; he has the potential to become one of the best, and he’d be a perfect fit in the Premier League, which, among other things, is Sylla’s dream destination.”

What aspects of his game still need improvement?

“It’s hard to say, especially since his growth in recent months has been impressive. I’d say he needs to gain more experience, which will come simply by playing. So I don’t see many things he needs to improve to take the next step in his career.”

Do you think Union Saint-Gilloise (USG) would be willing to let him leave in January, or do you think any transfer discussions will be postponed until the summer?

“I don’t think USG will let him leave in January. The only possible scenario, which I don’t think will happen, but which is the only solution anyway, is for USG to sign him in January but keep him at least until the end of the season, especially since the club never sells its best players in January.

“I also think interested clubs could spend a lot of money, but Union won’t let him leave in January.”

Could you describe him in three adjectives?

“Quick, physical, and full of character, because he’s someone who always has problems when he has to make decisions.”

“Considering his development, I’d say Pacho. He came from nowhere in Belgium, developed, moved to Frankfurt, and then ended up at PSG. In Sylla’s case, I think he’ll go straight to the Premier League. He has everything it takes to be perfect for this league.”

He’s still very young. Do you think he’s ready to play for a big club in a big city like Milan?

“He’s still very young, but he’s humble, calm, and we mustn’t forget that he arrived last year, in January, from the Norwegian second division. He played very little last year, but he’s very strong mentally and has started this season as if he’s been playing with this team for years.

“I can’t imagine USG without Sylla today, especially since we’re talking about one of the best defenders in the league. At the end of the season, he’ll make a significant leap in his career, but in my opinion it won’t be AC ​​Milan because he’s waiting for the Premier League. And from what I know, several English clubs are already ready to make him a player.

“So AC Milan could give him a try, but it will require a big project and a lot of money.”

We shall have to see how January develops and whether he could be sold on the project. However, it certainly doesn’t bode well from these comments.

#1827. Tottenham injury update: Mathys Tel, James Maddison, Mykhailo Mudryk latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham return to Premier League action on Saturday, but those fitness concerns heading into the international break remain ahead of a visit from Ipswich.

Defeat to Leeds last time out not only halted Spurs’ momentum after three straight wins and a draw, but it was a costly one for Mathys Tel as he left Elland Road wearing a protective boot and needing the aid of crutches.

There has since been an update on the French youngster, and not a positive one at that. Furthermore, James Maddison’s fitness has been called into question after twice failing to be called upon from the bench this month.

However, there is better news on the likes of Savio, Lucas Bergvall and, potentially, Xavi Simons.

Here is all the latest Tottenham injury news and return dates.

Mathys Tel could be out for a significant period after suffering a “bad injury” during the defeat at Leeds, which left him on crutches after the game.

The forward was on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from Leeds defender Jayden Bogle, who landed with his studs up on the Frenchman’s left Achillies but escaped even a booking for the foul despite a VAR review.

Despite initially trying to play on, Tel eventually signalled to come off and was replaced by Dominic Solanke. The young striker was later seen leaving Elland Road on crutches and with a protective boot on as he made his way to Spurs’ team bus.

As confirmed by French Football Federation (FFF), Tel did not link up with the France U21s as a result of the injury, meaning he missed the loss to Italy and will sit out Tuesday's showdown with England.

A statement reads: “Having suffered an injury with his club Tottenham, Mathys Tel is forced to withdraw from the France Under-21 team training camp which began this Monday at the CNF Clairefontaine.”

It still remains to be seen how long Tel will be sidelined for, with a further update likely to follow during the De Zerbi addresses the media in the pre-Ipswich press conference later this week.

Fitness concerns remain regarding James Maddison after failing to come off the bench in Tottenham’s last two games.

Maddison has not played since picking up an issue during the win at Chelsea last month, and De Zerbi opted to turn to teenager Lucas Williams-Barnett instead of the experienced midfielder with Spurs chasing a goal at Elland Road.

“James, I thought [about bringing him on] in the last substitution before Luca Williams-Barnett, but I saw [Mohammed] Kudus was very tired,” De Zerbi explained.

“And James didn’t [train] until Thursday. On Thursday he worked half [and] part of the training yesterday.

“And in the last 15 minutes maybe could be a good solution, but I decided to make that change because Luca in the winger position, is better than Maddison.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

There was slight hope that Savio would return for the trip Leeds, which would have been ahead of schedule.

This was after Savio was spotted training with his team-mates ahead of the game, having seemingly recovered from the muscular injury picked up against Manchester United last month.

However, the Brazilian was again absent heading into the international break.

The good news, though, is he could now be available against Ipswich, thus bolstering De Zerbi’s attacking options even further.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

Tosin Adarabioyo has been sidelined with a calf injury since making his first start of the season last month, in a win over Coventry, but was back in contention heading into the international break.

Tosin was not involved in the squad at Leeds, having only days earlier returned to first-team training.

De Zerbi said on Friday: “Tosin is available, yesterday he came inside with the group.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

Lucas Bergvall will be hoping to return from injury after the international break, after missing the last four games for Spurs with a knock.

The initial prognosis was a two-week absence, but now Bergvall will have a fortnight get back up to speed after being left out of Sweden’s latest squad.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

The reason for Martin Dubravka’s absence from the Tottenham squad against Leeds is down to a minor knee injury which prevented him from being named in the Slovakia squad for their Nations League double-header.

Spurs’ back-up goalkeeper is not expected to be sidelined for too long, so a return on the bench against Ipswich is likely.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

Signed on loan from Chelsea in the summer, Mudryk played just one game before picking up an ankle injury in training back in September.

De Zerbi stated the timeframe for the “stupid” injury was six to eight weeks, with it originally hoped that the Ukrainian could be involved by late October. That was then updated to after the Novemver international break.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

New reports suggest that Xavi Simons will enter the final phase of his recovery this month and return to first-team training, having only ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) back in April.

Simons suffered the injury against Wolves and was predicted to return early in 2027.

The Dutchman posted footage of himself training on the grass last month and his early comeback would be a massive boost for De Zerbi.

Frenchman Wilson Odobert is another Spurs player recovering from an ACL injury. The former Burnley man sustained his tear against Newcastle in February.

The typical timeframe for an ACL recovery would have the winger available to Spurs in December, but De Zerbi’s recent comments put that timeline under some doubt.

The Italian stated: “I don't know, because he has not started yet to work with us. I have no idea [when he will return].”

#1826. Mancini urges Italy to learn from Belgium thrashing amid Nations League near-miss

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto Mancini acknowledged that Belgium were by far the better side in Italy's 4-1 Nations League defeat, but vowed that his team would learn from the experience after they missed out on a quarter-final spot.

Italy went into Sunday's clash leading Group A1 and even took the lead at Stade Roi Baudouin through Francesco Pio Esposito, but then collapsed before half-time, shipping three goals within 11 minutes.

Maxim De Cuyper, Nathan Ngoy and Jeremy Doku led Belgium's comeback, with Diego Moreira striking late on to seal a spot in the quarter-finals at Italy's expense.

Pio Esposito also saw a penalty saved by Senne Lammens in the 91st minute as the Azzurri were forced to settle for a third-place finish following France's 2-1 win over Turkiye.

And Mancini wants his team to learn from missing out on qualification.

"They were better, we suffered too much on a physical level and in one-on-one situations," Mancini said.

"We started well, yes, but they were better on the night.

"When the ball got to the wings, we struggled to have the right pressing, they caused us problems.

"We felt some fatigue from the France match, but they deserved the victory, there's nothing more to say."

Belgium created chances worth 3.42 expected goals (xG) to Italy's 1.90 xG, aided in part by Pio Esposito's missed penalty late on.

Though his team were ultimately well beaten, Mancini feels Italy are on the right track as he begins a rebuild following their failure to qualify for the World Cup earlier this year.

"These nights can happen in the growth process, you need to learn from these experiences," Mancini continued.

"Considering the way we got here, we had the chance to qualify, but we knew it would be tough, as Belgium are a strong team.

"Of course we are sad now, but this night will help us going forward."
