#1807. Juventus keen on a January swoop for Tottenham’s Destiny Udogie

Juventus are closely monitoring Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie ahead of the January transfer window, according to a report from Ekrem Konur over the weekend.

Not included in Roberto De Zerbi’s squad for their 1-0 loss away at Leeds prior to November’s international break, Udogie has drastically failed to stake any kind of claim under the former Brighton boss this season.

Dealing with multiple injury setbacks and concerns over his fitness, the Italian international has made just a single Premier League start since a 0-0 stalemate away at Nottingham Forest on September 5th.

With summer arrival and former Liverpool star Andy Robertson immediately cementing his spot as De Zerbi’s number one choice at left-back, there were suggestions over the summer to Udogie was open to a permanent move away from north London.

However, failing to find any real stability since completing a £15million move from Serie A outfit Udinese back in 2022, the 12-cap international is reportedly firmly on Juventus’ radar.

Konur reported on Saturday that the Old Lady are closely monitoring Udogie’s situation in north London and are keen on a potential January swoop.

It has also been suggested that Juventus are hoping to agree an initial loan deal when the window reopens and have either an option or obligation included ahead of next summer.

#1806. Republic of Ireland vs Kosovo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 15 Nov 2026 11:44, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 14:05

Facing off for a UEFA Nations League playoff spot, the Republic of Ireland and Kosovo will clash at Dublin's Aviva Stadium on Tuesday night.

With the hosts trailing their visitors by one point in League B Group 3, the pair are vying for second place behind confirmed winners Austria.

Any hope of securing automatic promotion to Europe's top level was ended when Ireland lost in Austria on Saturday night, leaving them six points adrift of their hosts.

Ending the stubborn resistance of goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher, who produced a string of sharp saves throughout the match, substitute Sasa Kalajdzic notched a late winner in Linz.

As a result, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side sit third in Group 3, one point behind Kosovo, who they must now beat on the final matchday.

The stakes are quite high, as victory would ensure both a Nations League promotion playoff and entry to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

At the outset, Hallgrimsson highlighted how positive results in this campaign would aid Ireland's aim of reaching a Euros that will be partly played on home soil.

Another set of circumstances could instead send them into a relegation playoff against League C opponents - if they lose again and Israel defeat Austria, the Boys in Green will finish fourth.

Yet, having kicked off with a 1-0 loss in Pristina earlier this season, Ireland will welcome Kosovo to Dublin with an historic promotion still up for grabs.

After both sides endured agony in the World Cup playoffs, Kosovo came out on top in September's Group 3 opener, as Vedat Muriqi finally broke through with a late winner.

Franco Foda's team have made rapid progress in the Nations League, previously finishing second in their League C section, before winning both legs of a playoff against Iceland.

Now in Europe's second tier for the first time, Kosovo could soon ascend straight up to League A.

If they avoid defeat on Tuesday evening, the Balkan nation will guarantee entry to the promotion playoffs, which are set to take place in March.

Second spot would have been even more firmly within their grasp but for failing to beat Israel last time out, when Veldin Hodza was sent off in a 0-0 home draw.

Even so, having picked up a single point from three consecutive fixtures, one more will be enough to keep Kosovo's campaign alive.

Despite Ireland's loss in Linz, Hallgrimsson is likely to keep a settled side, although captain Nathan Collins has been ruled out by a knee injury.

John Egan, Jake O'Brien and Jimmy Dunne will all compete to replace the Brentford centre-back in a three-man defence.

After forming an attacking trident in recent games, Jack Moylan and Adam Idah should continue to support Troy Parrott up front.

The latter may have endured a dry spell with Real Betis, but he has scored 10 goals in his last eight competitive appearances for Ireland.

Meanwhile, Muriqi is set to spearhead Kosovo's front line, as their captain and all-time top scorer with 33 international goals - including one in the reverse fixture.

Como winger Mergim Vojvoda should feature in Muriqi's supporting cast, but Juventus forward Edon Zhegrova has just withdrawn due to injury.

Ermal Krasniqi and Lumbardh Dellova - both of Turkish Super Lig surprise package Amedspor - were already ruled out, while Hodza must serve a suspension.

Republic of Ireland possible starting lineup:

Kelleher; O'Shea, Egan, Scales; Abankwah, Molumby, Azaz, Manning; Moylan; Idah, Parrott

Saipi; Kamberi, I. Krasniqi, Raci, Gallapeni; Emerllahu, Avdullahu; Vojvoda, Rashica, Zabergja; Muriqi

September's loss in Pristina was one of only two in Ireland's last 13 matches, and the Boys in Green generally raise their game on home turf.

As Kosovo are missing some key men from a thin squad, they may suffer defeat in Dublin and slip down to third place.

#1805. ‘Exposed the world champions’: Spanish press react to England win in Nations League

10 man England secured a miraculous 3-2 win against world champions Spain in Madrid to top their Nations League group.

The Three Lions raced into a 3-0 lead at the Metropolitano Stadium, before Elliot Anderson conceded a penalty and was shown a straight red card for bringing down Lamine Yamal inside the area.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored the resulting spot-kick, and substitute Nico Williams set up a nervy finish as he slotted the ball home after a quick counter-attack.

Despite late pressure from Spain, England held on thanks to a superb double save from James Trafford, ending La Roja’s 43-game unbeaten run on a memorable night for Thomas Tuchel’s side.

Sunday’s result will go down as one of the most remarkable nights in England’s recent history, with Tuchel admitting his team reached the “highest level football-wise in all aspects of the game”.

Meanwhile, captain Harry Kane, who opened the scoring from the penalty spot at the end of the first half, said the victory was “as big as it gets” outside of a major tournament.

England entered the international break still carrying the scars of the World Cup, with Tuchel facing significant criticism for his in-game management during their semi-final defeat to Argentina.

However, victory over Spain means England have now won five of their six matches since returning from America, while Tuchel can point to having got his substitutions right as his side held on with 10 men to beat the reigning world and European champions in their own backyard.

England made the perfect start in the Spanish capital, with Declan Rice claiming post-match that, “The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played” as Luis de La Fuente’s side struggled to live with England’s pressing.

ITV pundit and former Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane was similarly impressed by England’s intense start, describing their first-half performance as “perfect” after Kane gave the visitors a deserved lead just before the break.

Keane’s ITV colleague, Ian Wright, was particularly pleased for Arsenal right-back Ben White, who was subjected to boos during England’s 2-1 victory over Croatia but started and scored against Spain after a flowing passing move.

“Can I just say, I’m really pleased for Ben White and the way things have turned around for him. It’s just brilliant for him to get back in, and he was magnificent tonight,” Wright said.

“There was a lot to be excited about for England. They were 3-0 up and cruising against the world champions before the red kind of changed the game.”

Spanish outlet AS also heaped praise on England’s performance, declaring the result as “the biggest setback of the De la Fuente era” with Tuchel’s men “completely neutralising Spain.”

“England exposed the world champions in what represents the biggest setback of the De la Fuente era, a bitter end to a dream 2026. Goals from Kane, Konsa, and White rewarded a superior opponent,” a report in AS stated.

“Credit goes to Tuchel, though his performance has been questioned because he seemed afraid to be the hero in the World Cup match against Argentina. It’s been a long time since an opponent has so thoroughly dismantled Spain.”

#1804. England winners and losers: Arsenal star rebuilding as Chelsea man suffers further setback

A terrific week for England ended with an away victory over Spain which Thomas Tuchel described as “like the Azteca reloaded”.

The Three Lions closed out their 2026 campaign by finishing top of their Nations League group thanks to a 2-1 win over Croatia last Thursday and then a heroic 10-man win in Madrid, 3-2, on Sunday.

While plenty of Tuchel’s players pushed their cases for further England involvement down the line, there were others who will feel less positive about the past week in terms of what it means for them.

Here, Standard Sport considers the winners and losers from England’s impressive autumn week.

Ben White has scored only 12 goals in his senior career but two have been for England, including the eventual winner in a famous win in Madrid.

Five years after his England debut, his first competitive start for his country came in Spain, and he didn’t disappoint.

The Arsenal man followed up a cameo against Croatia with one of England’s standout performances at the Estadio Metropolitano, defending robustly against Spain’s attacks down the left and then chipping in with that overlapping run and finish to make it 3-0.

Has had to field booing from sections of England fans since his return to the international fold in March after he walked away from their World Cup squad in 2022, but is rebuilding his England career successfully and will be thought of by Tuchel as one of his most well-balanced right-back options now.

Hopes to climb above Reece James and become first choice.

England’s left-back position changed hands a few times during the World Cup as Nico O’Reilly and Djed Spence battled it out mid-tournament, but that only served to make Tuchel’s decision to leave Hall behind appear all the more strange.

Hall has come back stronger and this month backed up his encouraging displays from the last international break.

Solid in the 2-1 win over Croatia, he was on another level entirely in Madrid, taking care of the threat of Lamine Yamal and finding a perfect balance between defence and attack as he helped England to victory in the world champions’ own backyard.

At the end of the last international break, when Trafford and Jordan Pickford split the four games two each, Pickford could no longer claim to be uncontested as England No1.

And after his heroics in Spain, even more so there is a debate to be had over whether it is time for England’s first-choice goalkeeper to be Leeds United’s Trafford rather than his Everton counterpart.

Arsenal star confronted as tempers flare during Spain vs England

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Pickford has never let England down in 94 caps, but Trafford made a string of stellar saves in Madrid and is eight years his junior.

Tuchel will likely continue to share the game time between them until he is pulled strongly enough in either direction. Trafford is making a very strong case for Pickford’s nine years without a genuine challenger to end with the shirt changing hands.

The Bayer Leverkusen defender has become accustomed to the bulk of his England game time being at right-back during this calendar year, but a shortage of centre-back options this month saw him start in the middle in both games

Quansah was solid for the most part but switched off in both games. And both errors were punished.

First he attempted a header back to Pickford from a Croatia corner that gifted the visitors a leveller at Wembley, then he dawdled on the ball long enough for Spain to intercept and race through; Elliot Anderson’s last-man red card and a Spain penalty followed.

Tuchel will hope he is stronger for the mistakes he made, but 23-year-old Quansah will be disappointed as he heads back to Germany.

Arguably it is harsh to include a player who was not even involved in the two matches, but the reason for Cole Palmer’s absence this month spoke volumes.

After dropping out of the last camp due to load management and being told by Tuchel that he “misses too many opportunities” to play for his country, this time the Chelsea talisman was not even selected.

Already faces huge competition in the No10 role but now there seems to be something of a repair job required if he is to get back into the fold and into Tuchel’s plans.

The 28-year-old is approaching 40 caps but his England career has been a strange old saga, really. Only Lee Carsley has ever appeared to truly trust him; Gareth Southgate and now Tuchel, less so.

Not in favour at Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho, his England game time across the autumn has felt a result of Reece James’s injuries and evidence right-back is a problem position more than it has an opportunity earned through strong club form.

Categorising Alexander-Arnold as a sublime passer who is suspect defensively became cliché long ago — yet being pinched of the ball in a poor area by Croatia was just the latest confirmation.

England managers have lacked the faith required to start him in England’s toughest matches for years now, and so it continued as he remained an unused substitute in Madrid.

White is just the latest player to climb above him in the pecking order.

#1803. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

The English forward joined Chelsea from Borussia Dortmund last summer for just under £50m. He struggled to make an impact last season in his first year at Chelsea, failing to register a goal in the Premier League or Champions League but did spend most of the second half of last season on the sidelines due to an injury. Gittens, who is on the bench for Chelsea today, has been speaking this week to CFC+:

“I am feeling, I would say, more confident now, in my body as well. The injury that happened [impacted my first season], but I am feeling better every day. I am trying to improve every day to be the best version of myself. It has been good to be back with the boys. I am really enjoying it right now and it has been really good to be part of this team.”

Have a great day, Jamie. 🥳 pic.twitter.com/QeX83XrXAM

In Chelsea’s defeat to Juventus in midweek, Ukrainian forward Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 after a long doping ban was resolved. You can read all about that game right here. Mudryk is on the bench for Chelsea today.

Our line-up to face AC Milan! pic.twitter.com/MK2hd0c708

The team news is in from Jakarta! 🗞️ pic.twitter.com/BRBjmlgwz8

The atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Christian Pulisic and Goncalo Ramos will both be in action for their respective national sides tonight, heading into the games with different targets.

The international break isn’t exactly the most enjoyable period as a club supporter. However, the one comfort is that we can watch some of the players in action for their international sides, especially in Milan’s case as 13 players have been called up.

This evening, the likes of Pulisic (United States) and Ramos (Portugal) could get some playing time. The feeling is that they will have different targets for the games, though, given how their respective form has been with Milan.

#1801. Prediction: Gremio vs Bahia

Two camps who will mark their respective returns from November’s international break in the early hours of Thursday, Gremio will welcome Bahia to the Rio Grande do Sul.

With Europe’s elite domestic leagues all stealing centre stage this weekend, there are plenty of eye-catching betting promotions available.

Ahead of the midweek showdown from Porto Alegre, you can find all of the key Gremio vs Bahia H2H stats here.

Starting with the hosts, while some in Gremio’s camp might have opened up the 2026 campaign dreaming of the opportunity to mount a genuine Copa Libertadores charge, Renato Portaluppi’s men have endured a public Serie A struggle this season. Marking their return from November’s international break sat in the relegation zone, the Immortal Tricolor have plenty of pressure on their shoulders ahead of Thursday’s showdown in Porto Alegre. However, last seen punching their spot in the final of this season’s Copa do Brasil thanks to a 3-1 aggregate victory against Atletico Mineiro, Gremio have enjoyed an essential recent upturn in fortune. Signing off October with a 2-0 win at home against Athletico-PR, Thursday’s hosts have lost just one of their previous five domestic appearances across all competitions. Likewise, Portaluppi’s camp have registered back-to-back victories in Porto Alegre for the first time since the start of September.

Shown what was a costly booking against reigning Serie A champions Flamengo earlier in the month, veteran defender Walter Kannemann will serve a one-match suspension here. However, serving his own top-flight ban on November 4th, one-time Tottenham striker Carlos Vinicius should be handed an immediate full Serie A recall.

Despite registering just a sole top-flight strike so far this season, former Barcelona star Martin Braihwaite will be hoping to keep his spot from the start. Completing a permanent switch to Porto Alegre over the summer, Croatian international Filip Krovinovic could make a first start since October 11th.

As for the visitors, while Bahia might have signed off October with a much-welcomed 3-2 victory at home against Sao Paulo, Rogerio Ceni’s men were searching for some essential stability prior to November’s international break. Last seen making an immediate return to losing ways as they eventually fell to a dramatic 3-2 loss against Cruzeiro, the Salvador-based outfit now have a major battle on their hands in the race to punch a Copa Libertadores ticket over the next month. Marking their return in midweek holding just a two-point buffer over sacrificing their spot, Bahia have mustered just a single win from any of their previous five appearances across all competitions. With their recent struggles underlined by a 3-0 drumming against Flamengo on October 18th, Thursday’s guests have shown some extended defensive issues.

Still recovering from a long-term knee injury and not making a single appearance across all competitions since the end of May, veteran goalkeeper Leo Vieira remains on the sidelines. However, despite struggling to hold down a regular spot this season, ex-Real Betis striker Willian Jose could return to Ceni’s squad.

Bagging what turned out to be a consolation strike against Cruzeiro prior to November’s international break, Alejo Veliz should keep his spot leading the line. Former New York City midfielder Nicolas Acevedo will start in the middle of the park here.

Looking to skyrocket their way out of the drop zone, Gremio will be bracing themselves for what could be a season-defining showdown in the early hours of Thursday. Last seen in Porto Alegre landing a deserved 2-0 win against Atletico Mineiro, the Immortal Tricolor will be boosted by their recent success on home soil. Landing back-to-back victories in front of their own supporters for the first time since the start of September, they will be looking to exploit a Bahia squad who have shown some extended issues on their travels.

#1800. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the five teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, as things currently stand, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

Portugal’s position in Group A4 is still to be confirmed after they were humbled at home by Denmark in their first game since Cristano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

#1799. Mexico vs Jamaica - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 15 Nov 2026 11:49, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 11:49

Mexico play host to Jamaica in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie on Tuesday night.

Jamaica hold a 3-2 advantage from the opening fixture over the weekend as the Reggae Boys attempt to cause a major surprise in this competition.

With Jamaica having finished second behind Guatemala in their group, Mexico would have been confident of earning an advantage from Saturday's first leg in Kingston.

Instead, Mexico are fortunate to still be competitive in the tie having found themselves 3-0 down by the 63rd minute.

Two goals in the closing 20 minutes kept the World Cup last-16 representatives in the tie, yet Rafael Marquez remains without a win as manager.

The former defender has now overseen two draws and three draws, with El Tri having lost 3-0 and 2-0 to USA and Chile respectively prior to their latest fixture.

As defending champions, it would be a major knock on Marquez should he fail to guide Mexico to at least the last four of the competition.

Meanwhile, Jamaica are attempting to move closer to a second semi-final appearance in three Nations League campaigns.

Having lost out to DR Congo in the World Cup playoffs earlier in the year, Rudolph Speid's side have delivered a strong response.

Although two defeats have been posted in seven games, they defeated El Salvador and earned a draw with Honduras on away territory before Saturday's five-goal thriller.

Jamaica had failed to win their previous six games against Mexico before that contest, emphasising the magnitude of the result.

Kevin Alvarez, Santiago Sandoval, Jesus Corona and Alexis Vega are all in contention for Mexico having helped inspire the comeback during the closing quarter of the first leg.

Despite his role as captain, Cesar Montes could be among those to drop down to the substitutes' bench, along with forward Santiago Gimenez.

Eighteen-year-old Gilberto Mora should keep his spot in a creative midfield role.

As for Jamaica, Denzel Hall may be handed a start over Kyle Ming at right wing-back.

However, Speid could be against making further changes to his side, unless he shows preference towards introducing fresh legs.

Javon East has started the last three games down the middle of the attack.

Rangel; Alvarez, Reyes, Vasquez, Gallardo; Romo, Lira, Mora; Corona, Vega, Quinones

Waite; Latibeaudiere, Freckleton, King; Hall, Anderson, Clarke, Webster; Dixon, East, Cephas

Despite holding an advantage, we expect Jamaica to try to play their normal game in Guadalupe. However, that may play into the hands of Mexico, who we are backing to qualify for the semi-finals with a decisive late goal.

#1798. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1797. Watch: Arsenal star Ben White confronted amid heated tunnel bust-up during Spain vs England

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal stars found themselves at the centre of a dispute as England and Spain players clashed at half-time of their Nations League showdown.

Gunners defensive duo Ben White and Ezri Konsa were on the scoresheet for the Three Lions, helping their side to a famous 3-2 win away in Spain.

England, however, had to see out the final 30 minutes with a man disadvantage as Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson was shown a red card for fouling Lamine Yamal inside the box.

Despite that, Thomas Tuchel’s side held on for three points that lifted them above Spain in their Nations League group.

The other major talking point in the Spanish capital was an incident that occurred at half-time, when White clashed with Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian Ruiz as the pair walked off the pitch.

This lead to a pouring of white and red shirts. David Raya, back-up to Unai Simon while on international duty, joined Arsenal team-mate Konsa in calming matters.

Martin Zubimendi also attempted to play peacemaker after initially getting involved, conversing with Konsa as the huddle moved towards the tunnel.

A sixth Arsenal player was close by, as Mikel Merino - moments away from being hauled off at half-time - watched on as the argument fizzled out.

There were a total of eight Arsenal players involved in the matchday squads for both nations. Eberechi Eze was an unused sub on the England bench, with his club teammate Myles Lewis-Skelly introduced in the second half as Tuchel looked to see out victory for the Three Lions.

Arsenal wingers Noni Madueke and Bukayo Saka are England regulars, but missed out on the squad for the last international break of 2026.

The Gunners return to action this weekend, when they travel to face Newcastle on Saturday, November 21.

#1795. Zidane ‘frustrated’ by sluggish first half despite France victory

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Zinedine Zidane was frustrated with France's first-half performance against Turkiye but was pleased to see them return to their style after the break to secure the win.

France finished their Nations League campaign with a 2-1 win over Turkiye, securing top spot in Group A1 as they qualified for the quarter-finals, finishing above Belgium.

An Emirhan Topcu own goal shortly after the break put France ahead, before Junior Kroupi's first international goal made sure of the points as Abdulkerim Bardakci netted a late consolation.

It was a much-needed win for France, who had suffered a 3-1 loss to Italy last time out – Zidane's first defeat in charge – to take the fight for a quarter-final place to the last game.

Les Bleus have now gone 10 matches without leading at half-time, dating back to the World Cup last 16 against Sweden (1-0 at half-time).

And though Zidane was disappointed by the sluggish first 45 minutes, he was much happier with Les Bleus' second-half showing.

"The objective was to qualify, possibly even finish first," Zidane told TF1.

"However, regarding the performance, we can be a little perplexed, especially our pressing in the first half. When you don't see certain things on the pitch, you get a bit frustrated.

"It's mainly about the pressing, because we allowed space to be created, and we weren't good at all with our pressing. We corrected that at half-time, and we were better afterwards.

"These are things we still need to improve. I wasn't happy, and neither were the players. But we corrected it.

"We conceded a lot, especially in the first half. In other matches, that was very rare. It's not just our defence; it's all of us together.

"It's not one or two players; it's things we have to put in place. We have to apply pressure as a team. We need to keep possession.

"We like to run with the ball, not without it; that's not our style. We did it better in the second half; we have to repeat that."

France were dominant against Turkiye, who finished bottom of the group after losing all six of their matches.

Les Bleus finished with 23 shots worth 3.4 expected goals (xG) and had five big chances overall.

However, they also gave up 13 attempts at the other end, with Turkiye generating 1.6 xG, and defender Jeremy Jacquet noted how vital the half-time team talk was in the result.

"The coach told us at half-time that he didn't think we were aggressive enough when we lost possession, and we corrected that in the second half," Jacquet said.

#1794. Spain boss Luis de la Fuente issues warning after Nations League defeat to England

Luis de la Fuente has stated the “best is yet to come” from Spain following their loss to England.

England’s 3-2 victory away in Madrid on Sunday evening ended Spain’s run of 43 straight games without defeat, handing the World Cup winners their first loss since March 2024.

Under De La Fuente, Spain have won a European Championship, a World Cup and a Nations League title in 2023 - as well as reaching the final of the latter in 2025.

However, defeat to England means that Spain will enter the quarter-finals stage of the 2026-27 Nations League as an unseeded runner-up, potentially setting up a showdown with France in March next year.

Reflecting on the game, De La Fuente said: “In the first 30 minutes, they knocked us out of our rhythm and were better than us. After that, we fought back, and I thought we were going to get the draw.

“But I’ll use a phrase that I’ve used before when we were unbeaten: ‘The best is yet to come’.”

De La Fuente also shared his belief that England approached the game in Madrid as a ‘final’, with Spain not as motivated for the game - which allowed the Three Lions to ‘trample’ over La Roja.

"The fact that the whole world wants to beat Spain is a great feeling,” he added. “This was a 'final', and in this type of game, you have to be spot on, in great shape, and if not, then an opponent like England, France, Portugal or Italy can trample all over you.”

The Spanish head coach went on to state that his side’s ambitions of winning the Nations League remained in place, with his side ‘determined’ to make amends.

He continued: "We'll try to be exactly the same in defeat as we were in victory. Okay, we haven't often tasted defeat, but we stay proud; we stay determined - in March, we're in the quarter-finals, and we'll go to those knockouts with the intention of winning, and winning the tournament."

#1793. Michael Olise: Bayern Munich's £265m valuation revealed amid Real Madrid links

By Naim Beneddra | 15 Nov 2026 12:06, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 17:13

Bayern Munich have reportedly placed an extraordinary valuation on Michael Olise as they look to discourage Real Madrid and other European heavyweights from pursuing the former Crystal Palace winger.

According to Spanish publication AS, the Bundesliga champions now value the France international at a staggering €300m (£265m), despite remaining determined to secure his long-term future at the Allianz Arena.

The figure would comfortably exceed the current world-record transfer fee of €222m (£198m), which Paris Saint-Germain paid Barcelona for Neymar in 2017.

Olise has attracted attention from several major European clubs since leaving Crystal Palace for Bayern in a €53m (£45m) deal in the summer of 2024, with Real Madrid among his reported admirers.

However, the German giants are in no hurry to entertain offers for their 24-year-old attacker, who remains under contract until June 2029.

The reported valuation is not an official release clause, nor does it indicate that Bayern are actively looking to sell Olise. Instead, it reflects the exceptionally high price that would potentially be required to persuade the club to consider his departure.

Olise has established himself as one of Europe's most productive attacking players since arriving in Germany, and his performances have strengthened Bayern's determination to retain his services.

The Frenchman registered 22 goals and 29 assists across all competitions last season, helping Bayern retain their Bundesliga crown and earning recognition as the league's Player of the Season.

He has continued that form into the 2026-27 campaign, contributing 12 goals and seven assists in 15 club appearances.

His ability to operate from the right flank, cut inside onto his stronger left foot and create opportunities for teammates has made him a central figure in Vincent Kompany's attacking system.

Bayern are consequently keen to reward Olise with an improved contract, despite having more than two-and-a-half years remaining on his current agreement.

The club have reportedly explored extending his deal until 2032, with a substantial salary increase that could place him alongside Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala among Bayern's highest earners.

However, discussions have yet to produce an agreement.

Previous reports have suggested that Olise's representatives want a release clause included in any new Bayern contract, potentially allowing the player greater control over a future move.

A figure of around £170m has been mentioned in connection with that proposed clause, considerably below Bayern's newly reported valuation.

Those demands remain part of the negotiations rather than agreed contractual terms.

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness has publicly played down concerns over the lack of progress, suggesting that the club have sufficient time to reach an agreement.

"The time will come to reach a new agreement. He has two more years on his contract," Hoeness was quoted as saying by AS.

Sporting director Christoph Freund has also insisted that Bayern are under no immediate pressure to extend the Frenchman's deal, praising Olise's development and reaffirming the club's satisfaction with his performances.

The German champions therefore appear determined to negotiate from a position of strength rather than allow speculation over his future to dictate their decisions.

Real Madrid's interest in Olise has been widely reported, with the Spanish giants previously considering the Frenchman as a potential addition to their attacking options.

The former Reading and Crystal Palace player attracted particular attention following his performances against Madrid in the Champions League, further enhancing his reputation among Europe's elite.

However, AS indicates that Real Madrid are not currently involved in active discussions over the player's future, despite the persistent links.

The emergence of Yan Diomande at the Santiago Bernabeu has also changed the composition of Madrid's attack, potentially reducing the urgency of pursuing another expensive wide forward.

Nevertheless, Olise's technical qualities and versatility make him an attractive long-term option for a club accustomed to recruiting leading attacking talent.

Any attempt to secure his signature would now face an enormous financial obstacle.

Bayern's reported €300m valuation represents almost six times the amount they paid Crystal Palace just over two years ago and would establish a new benchmark in the transfer market.

It is also substantially higher than the approximately €200m (£176m) valuation previously discussed in connection with the player's future.

The Bavarian club's position comes at a time when Olise's contractual demands are already attracting attention, with his future previously linked to Bayern's wider wage structure and Kane's status.

There is currently no indication that Madrid are prepared to meet Bayern's valuation, and the Bundesliga champions have not publicly invited bids for their star winger.

With Olise tied to Bayern until 2029, the club can continue pursuing an extension without facing the immediate prospect of losing him for a reduced fee.

For Real Madrid, the reported price reinforces the scale of the challenge involved in convincing Bayern to part with one of their most valuable players ahead of the summer 2027 transfer window.

#1791. Thomas Tuchel and Spain manager agree on England verdict after famous Nations League win

England goalkeeper James Trafford has been singled out for praise from both managers after the heroic 3-2 win over Spain.

Thomas Tuchel’s side finished top of their Nations League group above the world champions on goal difference after they avenged September’s 3-2 defeat at Wembley with victory by the same scoreline in Madrid.

England played the last half an hour with 10 men following Elliot Anderson’s red card.

Tuchel handed Jordan Pickford and Trafford two matches each during the last international break and again split their game time, with the Everton stopper playing in Thursday’s 2-1 win over Croatia and Trafford coming into the team against Spain.

The Leeds shot-stopper made a string of crucial saves late in the game as 10-man England held on for a famous win that brought an end to Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run.

Trafford’s double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte was particularly eye-catching, and his team-mates immediately mobbed him to praise him for those smart stops in added time.

The performance of the 24-year-old - vying with Pickford for the No1 shirt ahead of Euro 2028 - drew praise not only from Tuchel but also from his opposite number, the Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente.

“We did generate some chances, but England’s goalkeeper produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes,” De la Fuente said afterwards.

“I want to say how fantastic England were on the night,” he added.

Trafford’s own head coach was similarly impressed by the Leeds man’s influence on a high-stakes clash at the Metropolitano Stadium.

“The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end,” Tuchel said.

“Absolutely brilliant. There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

“Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half. [Along] with everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.”

Asked whether Trafford had closed the gap to long-time No1 Pickford, Tuchel said: “[He was] very good. That is his job: to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.”

#1790. Rwanda vs Mali - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 12:40, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 13:17

The top two teams in Group K of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers face off at Stade Amahoro on Tuesday as Rwanda host Mali.

This is the second meeting between the sides in four days, after Mali edged a 3-2 victory in Bamako last Friday.

Rwanda entered the clash at Stade du 26 Mars on a five-match unbeaten run - four of which were wins - and with the chance to move top of their AFCON qualifying group. They appeared set to do so after goals from Jojea Kwizera and Phanuel Kavita, only for a late collapse to result in a 3-2 defeat.

Beyond missing out on a crucial three points, Stephen Constantine’s men squandered the chance to claim their first victory over Mali in five attempts, a result that would have provided a major psychological boost ahead of the rematch in Kigali.

Amavubi will be eager to return to winning ways and avoid leaving their AFCON hopes in the balance ahead of the final round of qualifiers next March.

Victory on Tuesday could move Rwanda six points clear in the race for a place at the 2027 finals, but defeat could see them slip behind Cape Verde, who are now just behind after their win over Liberia.

Tuesday’s hosts are unbeaten at home since October, keeping clean sheets in three of their last four matches. Another solid defensive display - having never kept a shutout against Mali - would be a key step toward ending their winless run in this fixture.

Like Rwanda, Mali are also in the early stages of a new managerial era, and Anthony da Silva has made an impressive start at the helm - going unbeaten in his first four matches since taking over in June following Tom Saintfiet’s departure.

The most recent of those came against Rwanda last time out, as Les Aigles demonstrated their ability to win matches in different ways by securing their first comeback victory since eliminating 10-man Tunisia at the most recent Africa Cup of Nations.

One of only four teams still boasting a perfect record in the current qualifiers, Mali can move within touching distance of a place at the 2027 AFCON finals, where they will look to extend their run of 10 consecutive tournament appearances dating back to 2008.

Much of that success is due to Mali’s impressive qualifying record, having won five straight and gone 11 matches unbeaten since June 2023 (W9, D2) - a run bettered only by Morocco on the continent in that span.

Not since November 2021 have Tuesday’s visitors won four straight competitive matches, handing them the opportunity to make more history under a manager who has wasted no time stamping his authority on proceedings.

Rwanda Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mali Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Jojea Kwizera was directly involved in both of Rwanda’s goals last time out, and the 27-year-old will be eager to make an impact once again.

Djihad Bizimana has featured in all of his side’s AFCON qualifiers since November 2019 - a streak set to continue on Tuesday.

Ousmane Camara was forced off with an injury late in Mali’s last outing, making the centre-back a doubt for this fixture.

If Camara is unavailable, Cheick Keita could be handed his first competitive start at the heart of the defence.

Lassine Sinayoko has registered five goals and five assists in his last ten appearances for club and country. The Paris FC forward, who set up Moussa Kounfolo Yeo’s equaliser in Bamako, will be aiming to get back on the scoresheet.

Ntwari; Niyomugabo, Kavita, Mutsinzi, Byiringiro; Iradukunda, Bizimana, Ruboneka, Kwizera; Mickels, Biramahire

Diarra; Traore, Camara, Gassama, Guindo; Sangare, Haidara; Yeo, Doumbia, Nene; Sinayoko

As with last week’s encounter, there is little to separate the sides, so another tightly contested match is expected.

Mali’s superior quality proved decisive in the reverse fixture, but we expect Rwanda to claim a point this time and avoid falling six points adrift of their visitors.

#1789. ‘The decision is entirely his’ – Van Bommel denies advising De Bruyne on PSV move

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Belgium boss Mark van Bommel denied reports he has advised Kevin De Bruyne to consider a January move to PSV, insisting "the decision is entirely his".

PSV have reportedly made contact with De Bruyne, who is believed to be unhappy at Napoli, where his contract expires in June.

It was speculated Van Bommel had encouraged the midfielder to join PSV, where he won four league titles and made over 270 appearances across two spells.

However, Van Bommel clarified his stance following Sunday's 4-1 win over Italy, which booked the Red Devils' place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

"I was asked a question by a Belgian reporter about whether De Bruyne would fit in with the PSV style of play, and seeing as I know the club well," Van Bommel told Sky Sport Italia.

"I said yes he would, but he also fits in at Napoli. So, I answered a specific question, but I did not advise him to do anything. The decision is entirely his, and I leave that to him."

Qualification secured! https://t.co/qb15ckncDI

— Belgian Red Devils (@BelRedDevils) November 15, 2026

Belgium headed into their final Group A1 clash occupying third place, a point behind leaders Italy, who took the lead through Pio Esposito.

However, three goals in 11 first-half minutes from Maxim De Cuyper, Nathan Ngoy and Jeremy Doku flipped the contest on its head, before Diego Moreira added a fourth 10 minutes from time.

The Red Devils bettered their 3.42 xG, yet Van Bommel insists the margin of victory would have been greater but for good goalkeeping from Italy's Gianluigi Donnarumma.

"If Donnarumma had not been in goal, then we would've scored six," he added.

"I'll be honest, I didn't expect [to qualify] when we started two months ago. But even before that first match with Italy [September's 2-0 win], I could tell this was a really intelligent group of players. That makes it a pleasure for a coach to work with them."

#1788. Cardinale says pre-season is ‘up to Amorim’ as Milan will not chase ‘extra two million’

Gerry Cardinale has provided some refreshing comments on Milan’s pre-season plans for the future, confirming that money will no longer dictate where they go.

Over the last ten years or so, it has become far more common for big clubs to travel across the world for their pre-season campaigns. For example, Milan have been in Australia for two consecutive pre-seasons now, taking on Perth Glory and most recently Inter.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While it’s great to connect with local fan bases, the travel is demanding for the players. This summer, Milan played games in Glasgow (Scotland), Perth (Australia), Jakarta (Indonesia), and Wroclaw (Poland). resulting in a lot of travel.

Speaking about the pre-season in his long interview with Gazzetta dello Sport, Cardinale said that the upcoming pre-season planning will be decided by Ruben Amorim. Money will no longer dictate where they go. Instead, the best plan for preparing the players will be chosen.

In an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

“We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

“It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

“Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”
